'To speak power you must first *balance* stillness and intention,' she said. 'Let one tip the other and the vessel falls.' I stood very still. The ink glowed brighter with each slow breath.
balance:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊要我手背托着词器，说修炼者必须____静止与意志，才能驾驭词力。
balance:0.hook: A hairline crack appeared in the vessel's rim.
balance:0.line: 'To speak power, you must first *balance* stillness and intention.'

baby:0.en: Shen Wujiu laughed — kindly — when I mispronounced the third formula. 'Every master was once a *baby* of words,' he said, handing back my scroll. 'The sect does not expect your voice to be ready. It expects you to stay.' I read the formula again, slower. This time the characters on the wall did not flicker.
baby:0.cnHint: 师兄安慰我说，每位大师当初也是词语上的____，失败并不可耻。
baby:0.hook: But one character at the edge of the wall glowed red and would not settle.
baby:0.line: 'Every master was once a *baby* of words — stay, and you will grow.'

content:0.en: Inside the stone hall, rows of jade slips lined the shelves like sleeping stars. I pulled one free and read the word carved within: 'still.' Master Qingwu watched from her seat. 'You look *content*,' she said softly, 'but a calm face can hide a restless spirit.' I set the slip down. Outside, a single cloud drifted upward — against the wind.
content:0.cnHint: 在藏经堂内，我找到了心仪的玉简，师尊却说我脸上的____之色或许只是表象。
content:0.hook: The cloud that rose against the wind carried the shape of a warning hand.
content:0.line: 'You look *content*, but a calm face can hide a restless spirit.'

divide:0.en: Master Qingwu drew a line of pale light across the stone floor of the inner hall. 'This mark will *divide* your path,' she told me and Shen Wujiu. 'One side holds words of healing; the other holds words of force. Step to the side that calls you.' I moved left. Shen Wujiu moved left. The line began to glow red.
divide:0.cnHint: 师尊用光线将修炼之路一____为二，要求弟子各自选择，而那道线随后发出了红光。
divide:0.hook: Red light never meant welcome in the Cloud Sea Sect.
divide:0.line: 'This mark will *divide* your path — choose the side that calls you.'

generate:0.en: In the quiet of the ink room, I pressed my palm to the cold slate and tried to *generate* a single spark of word-flame. Sweat gathered at my brow. Xiaoxing had filled three slates by dawn; mine held only a smudge. Master Qingwu passed the doorway and did not stop — yet her sleeve brushed the candle, and the flame bent toward me like a pointing finger.
generate:0.cnHint: 在习字房中，我努力____出哪怕一点字焰，却远不及师妹，而烛火随后朝我弯折。
generate:0.hook: A flame that bends toward you is either a gift or a test.
generate:0.line: 'Can you *generate* even a spark before the candle burns out?'

operate:0.en: The sect's great wind-wheel stood at the center of the hall, its carved characters slowly turning. Shen Wujiu showed me how to *operate* it: press the root word, hold the tone, release on the third breath. When I tried, the wheel turned twice and stopped. A low hum filled the stone walls, and the dust on the floor formed a perfect circle around my feet.
operate:0.cnHint: 师兄教我如何____大风轮，但我操作时轮子中途停转，地上的尘埃却围着我画出了圆形。
operate:0.hook: Dust does not arrange itself — something watched, and left a mark.
operate:0.line: 'To *operate* the wheel, press the root word and hold your breath.'

properly:0.en: 'You have not *properly* learned the word for wind,' Master Qingwu said, without looking up from her brush. She was right. My strokes were wide, my tone unsteady, and twice the word had slipped from memory mid-breath. Xiaoxing placed a fresh slip on my desk without a word. Through the hall's narrow window, the sky had turned the color of old copper.
properly:0.cnHint: 师尊指出我尚未____掌握"风"字，师妹默默为我添了新玉简，窗外天色却变得异样。
properly:0.hook: Old-copper skies above the Cloud Sea never lasted past nightfall.
properly:0.line: 'You have not *properly* learned the word for wind — begin again.'

render:0.en: In the hall of seals, Shen Wujiu pressed two words together in the air and showed me how their joining could *render* a candle flame solid as glass, briefly touchable, painless. I tried with different words and felt the air thicken around my fingers. Then a third word slipped in, uninvited, and the flame went out entirely, leaving a faint scent of rain.
render:0.cnHint: 师兄演示如何将两字合一以____烛焰为可触之物，而我无意引入第三字后，焰光熄灭，留下雨气。
render:0.hook: Rain has no place inside a sealed hall — and yet, there it was.
render:0.line: 'The right pairing can *render* fire solid — but the wrong third word erases it.'

resolve:0.en: The morning test was simple: speak one word clearly enough to light the slate. I had failed twice. Xiaoxing caught my eye from across the room and gave a small nod. I felt a quiet *resolve* settle in my chest like a stone finding the bottom of a still pool. I spoke the word. The slate lit. Then every other slate in the row lit too, one by one, without being touched.
resolve:0.cnHint: 两次失败后，师妹的一个点头让我心中升起____之感，我终于点亮了石板，而后排石板也自动亮起。
resolve:0.hook: Slates do not light themselves — something in the room had listened.
resolve:0.line: 'Let your *resolve* settle before you speak — the word will follow.'

seemingly:0.en: The old scroll on Master Qingwu's desk was *seemingly* blank, its surface smooth and without a single mark. But when Shen Wujiu held it toward the window, faint characters appeared along the edge, thin as spider thread. Master Qingwu did not explain what they said. She simply rolled the scroll closed and placed it under my arm as I left the hall.
seemingly:0.cnHint: 师尊桌上那卷____空白的古卷，被师兄对着窗光一照，边缘显出细若蛛丝的字迹。
seemingly:0.hook: She gave no explanation — only a scroll that knew more than it showed.
seemingly:0.line: 'The scroll is *seemingly* empty — look again, with the light behind it.'

mix:0.en: Inside the preparation hall, I ground three dried herbs into fine powder and blended them together. Master Qingwu watched as I added the last pinch of silver dust, completing a careful *mix* of earth root, sky petal, and cloud moss. She said nothing, but her eyes held a quiet test.
mix:0.cnHint: 我在调药室里将三种灵草研磨后合为一体，师尊默默注视着这份____。
mix:0.hook: One ingredient, I feared, was not what it seemed.
mix:0.line: 'This *mix* must be exact, or the formula will reject you.'

necessity:0.en: Shen Wujiu placed a heavy scroll before me and crossed his arms. 'Reading is not pleasure here,' he said. I opened the first page and felt the weight of its meaning settle on me. The *necessity* of understanding each word before dawn was clear: without it, the morning test would end my path.
necessity:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，黎明前读懂卷轴是绝对的____，否则将无缘晨试。
necessity:0.hook: Outside, the cloud sea began to glow an unnatural red.
necessity:0.line: 'The *necessity* of this knowledge is not small — do not sleep.'

stuff:0.en: Xiaoxing pulled a worn cloth bag from beneath her sleeping mat and emptied it onto the stone floor. Dried petals, small vials, knotted cords — strange *stuff* she had gathered since her first year. She chose one pale vial and pressed it into my hand without a word, as if she had been waiting.
stuff:0.cnHint: 小星将她多年收集的各种____摊开在地，从中取出一支小瓶递给了我。
stuff:0.hook: The vial was warm, as though something inside it was breathing.
stuff:0.line: 'This *stuff* saved me once — keep it close tonight.'

translate:0.en: The old diagram on the inner wall was drawn in a script no one still spoke. Master Qingwu asked me to *translate* the first line aloud. I shaped each symbol into living words, and as I spoke the last one, a thin current of cold air moved through the sealed room with no open window.
translate:0.cnHint: 师尊要我将古老壁文____出来，当我念完最后一字，密室里无风自动。
translate:0.hook: The second line, I noticed, had my name written in it.
translate:0.line: 'Can you *translate* this glyph, or does it already know you?'

wander:0.en: I was told the library held ten thousand scrolls, but Master Qingwu had warned me to take only the one I was assigned. Still, my eyes began to *wander* across the shelves, drawn by faint light pulsing from a narrow gap between two heavy volumes no one else seemed to notice.
wander:0.cnHint: 我本该只取指定卷轴，但目光忍不住在书架间____，发现了一道陌生的微光。
wander:0.hook: The light blinked once, as if it had noticed me back.
wander:0.line: 'Do not let your mind *wander* — some shelves here listen.'

warn:0.en: Shen Wujiu stepped in front of me before I could touch the brass door at the end of the corridor. His voice was low and steady. He did not shout, but the weight in his words made me stop. He had come to *warn* me that the door only opened from the inside, and never opened twice.
warn:0.cnHint: 师兄拦住了我，专程来____我那扇铜门只开一次，且只能从里面打开。
warn:0.hook: Behind the door, something knocked, once and slowly.
warn:0.line: 'I *warn* you now because no one warned me then.'

advocate:0.en: During the sect's morning debate, a senior disciple argued that new members should be forbidden from the upper herb rooms. Master Qingwu stood and spoke against this calmly. She was a quiet but firm *advocate* for those who were still learning, and her words shifted the mood of every elder in the hall.
advocate:0.cnHint: 师尊在晨议上为新弟子发声，是我们坚定的____，改变了长老们的态度。
advocate:0.hook: One elder did not change expression, and that felt wrong.
advocate:0.line: 'I am an *advocate* for the new — let them try before you judge.'

cite:0.en: When I asked Master Qingwu why our sect followed such a difficult path to advancement, she did not explain in her own words. Instead, she chose to *cite* a single line from the founding record, brushed on the ceiling of the inner hall. I looked up, read it, and understood why easy paths were never trusted.
cite:0.cnHint: 师尊没有亲自解释，而是____了内殿天花板上创派记录中的一句话作为回答。
cite:0.hook: The line on the ceiling had been written in two different hands.
cite:0.line: 'When in doubt, *cite* those who built what we stand inside.'

teenager:0.en: The inner hall smelled of pine smoke and old scrolls. I stood before Master Qingwu, a *teenager* still uncertain of my own name in the sect's records. She studied my hands without a word, then placed a single silver leaf on my palm. Outside, wind moved through the chimes.
teenager:0.cnHint: 师尊在内殿审视这位刚入门的____，将一片银叶放在他掌心。
teenager:0.hook: The leaf began to tremble, though the air was still.
teenager:0.line: 'A *teenager* who listens to the wind already knows half the art.'

patient:0.en: Master Qingwu called me to the medicine room before dawn. A pale disciple lay on the low bench, breathing in shallow waves. 'Watch,' she said, pressing a green herb to his wrist. She was *patient*, moving without hurry, as if time itself waited for her hands to finish.
patient:0.cnHint: 师尊在药室里，____地为生病的弟子施法疗伤。
patient:0.hook: When the herb dissolved, the disciple's eyes opened — but they were the wrong color.
patient:0.line: 'Be *patient*; a formula forced is a formula broken.'

classroom:0.en: The sect's learning hall was nothing like I had imagined. The *classroom* was carved from a single hollow stone, its walls lined with glowing word-sigils instead of windows. Shen Wujiu sat cross-legged at the front, reciting a wind formula in a low, steady voice. Dust motes rose and held still above him.
classroom:0.cnHint: 弟子们在这间奇特的____中学习风诀，尘埃在空中静止不动。
classroom:0.hook: One sigil on the wall had begun to weep pale light.
classroom:0.line: 'In this *classroom*, every word you forget costs you altitude.'

vehicle:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long diagram on the table. 'A flying formula is not a gift,' she said. 'It is a *vehicle*; it carries only what you are willing to give.' I traced the lines with one finger and felt a faint hum travel up my arm and settle behind my eyes.
vehicle:0.cnHint: 师尊说飞升之诀是一种____，只承载修者愿意付出之物。
vehicle:0.hook: The hum did not stop even after I lifted my hand.
vehicle:0.line: 'A word used as a *vehicle* will take you exactly as far as your courage holds.'

remote:0.en: Xiaoxing spread a sect map across the reading desk and pointed to a pale mark near the edge. 'That grove is *remote*,' she said quietly. 'Three peaks beyond any patrol path.' The characters written there were so old they had nearly faded into the paper itself. No disciple was listed as having returned from it.
remote:0.cnHint: 晓星指着地图边缘那片____的林地，那里的文字古老得几近消隐。
remote:0.hook: Below the faded mark, someone had drawn a small, careful warning eye.
remote:0.line: 'The most *remote* place on this map is also the most watched.'

zoo:0.en: Shen Wujiu laughed when I described the spirit-beast courtyard to Xiaoxing. 'It is not a *zoo*,' he said from the doorway, arms folded. 'Every creature there holds a word inside its blood. You do not visit them. You study them.' Above the courtyard gate, a stone dragon's eye caught the morning light and held it.
zoo:0.cnHint: 师兄纠正道，灵兽院并非____，每只灵兽体内都藏有一个字。
zoo:0.hook: The stone dragon's other eye, I now noticed, was missing.
zoo:0.line: 'Call it a *zoo* again and the beasts will hear you — they remember insults.'

card:0.en: Before the rank trial, Master Qingwu handed each disciple a small jade *card* no larger than a thumb. Mine was warm and carried a single character I could not yet read. 'If the hall grows too dark,' she said, 'press it to your chest.' She did not say what would happen then.
card:0.cnHint: 试炼前，师尊给每位弟子一块刻有字符的玉____，并嘱咐在黑暗中贴于胸口。
card:0.hook: The character on my card shifted the moment she turned away.
card:0.line: 'This *card* holds one breath of my own cultivation — use it wisely.'

gene:0.en: Xiaoxing showed me a passage in the oldest text on the shelf. It said that a cultivator's gift was written in the body like a *gene*, passed from master to student through shared breath over years of practice. Master Qingwu had never spoken of this. I closed the book carefully and set it back exactly as I had found it.
gene:0.cnHint: 晓星发现古籍记载，修炼天赋如同____一般刻在身体里，由师徒间共同修行传递。
gene:0.hook: A single page near the back had been torn out, cleanly and long ago.
gene:0.line: 'If cultivation runs like a *gene*, then what did Master Qingwu inherit — and from whom?'

modern:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old cedar and dried cloud-moss. On a low table sat a single stone tablet, its surface carved with ancient words. 'We do not chase *modern* methods here,' Master Qingwu said, placing one hand on the cold stone. 'The oldest words carry the deepest breath.' I nodded, though my fingers itched to touch it.
modern:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，云海宗不追求____的修炼方法，古老的词语才是根本。
modern:0.hook: Behind the tablet, a hairline crack had begun to glow.
modern:0.line: 'We do not chase *modern* methods — the oldest words carry the deepest breath.'

officer:0.en: A visitor arrived at the sect gate before dawn: a tall man in grey robes bearing a bronze seal. Shen Wujiu whispered that the man was a court *officer*, sent to inspect all mountain sects for signs of forbidden word-craft. Master Qingwu received him without fear, offering only tea and silence. The officer left before the clouds lifted.
officer:0.cnHint: 一位朝廷____来到宗门检查，师尊以茶和沉默应对，对方悄然离去。
officer:0.hook: On the table where the tea had sat, a single character was burned into the wood.
officer:0.line: 'A court *officer* who fears silence has already lost the argument.'

convince:0.en: Xiaoxing had copied the wind-word seventeen times, yet it refused to rise from the page. She came to me, eyes bright with worry. 'I cannot *convince* the word to move,' she said softly. 'It sits there like a stone.' I told her to stop trying to push it and simply breathe alongside it. On the eighteenth copy, the paper lifted one corner.
convince:0.cnHint: 师妹无法____这个风字动起来，直到她停止强迫，随它呼吸，才出现了转机。
convince:0.hook: Outside, every candle in the hall bent toward her window at once.
convince:0.line: 'I cannot *convince* the word to move — it just sits there like a stone.'

directly:0.en: Master Qingwu set a small flame-word on the stone floor and told us to read it. Shen Wujiu stepped back, cautious. I walked *directly* toward it, crouching close until the heat pressed against my cheeks. The word pulsed once, twice, then printed itself faintly on my palm — warm and painless. Master Qingwu said nothing, but she smiled at the floor.
directly:0.cnHint: 师尊让我们靠近火字，我____走向它，它便将自己印在了我的手心。
directly:0.hook: The mark on my palm had not faded by the time the moon rose.
directly:0.line: 'Walk *directly* toward it — a word that senses fear will never open.'

extend:0.en: The lesson that morning was about reach. Master Qingwu drew a breath-word on rice paper and pressed it against the wall. 'A skilled disciple can *extend* a single word across an entire room,' she said. 'Fill the space slowly, like water.' I tried, and the word stretched thin — then held. Shen Wujiu exhaled beside me as if he had been holding his own breath all along.
extend:0.cnHint: 师尊教我们如何____一个字的力量，让它弥漫整个房间，就像水一样缓慢充满空间。
extend:0.hook: At the far wall, where the word had reached, the stone had turned faintly blue.
extend:0.line: 'A skilled disciple can *extend* a single word across an entire room — try.'

rat:0.en: A small *rat* had crept into the medicine room and chewed through a packet of sleep-words. By morning the whole lower hall was thick with quiet — birds outside had stopped, and two disciples had dozed off standing up. Xiaoxing found the creature curled asleep beside the empty packet, whiskers still. Master Qingwu only said the words had chosen their own student.
rat:0.cnHint: 一只____咬破了装着睡眠词语的纸包，导致整个厅堂陷入奇异的宁静。
rat:0.hook: When the rat finally woke, its eyes had turned the pale silver of a full moon.
rat:0.line: 'Even a *rat* that swallows a word without meaning becomes part of the lesson.'

saturday:0.en: The sect marked rest days by the old court calendar. On *Saturday*, no word-craft was permitted — brushes were set down, tablets covered with cloth. I sat by the inner window watching cloud-ships drift far below. Shen Wujiu brought two bowls of warm grain and said nothing for a long while. It was the most peaceful hour I had known since climbing the mountain.
saturday:0.cnHint: 在____这天，宗门禁止一切修炼，我和师兄静静地坐在窗边，看云海上的船影漂过。
saturday:0.hook: Then, from the covered tablets, a faint hum rose — low and steady as a held note.
saturday:0.line: 'On *Saturday* the words rest too — even they need silence to grow stronger.'

april:0.en: *April* on the floating mountain meant the cloud-sea turned green at the edges, as if spring had climbed up through the mist. Master Qingwu opened the archive room for the first time since I had arrived, saying that growth-words could only be read in this month. The room smelled of rain and old bark. I held the first scroll carefully, afraid the season might slip away before I reached the last line.
april:0.cnHint: ____时节，云海泛出绿意，师尊打开了封存已久的档案室，说生长词语只有这个月才能被解读。
april:0.hook: The last character on the scroll was still wet, as though written that very morning.
april:0.line: 'Only in *April* do the growth-words wake — read quickly before the month turns.'

store:0.en: Inside the Sect's inner hall, rows of jade shelves held every kind of spiritual herb. Master Qingwu called this the *store* of the Sect — a living treasury where each plant carried a word of power. I counted the jars, feeling the hum of ten thousand names pressing against the glass.
store:0.cnHint: 师父带我参观内堂的草药____，每一株植物都蕴含着字符之力。
store:0.hook: One jar was warm — and it had no label.
store:0.line: 'This *store* holds every word the Sect has ever mastered,' said Master Qingwu.

budget:0.en: Master Qingwu spread a long scroll across the low table. Each line recorded how much spiritual energy a disciple might spend in a single season. 'Your *budget* of power is not endless,' she said, tracing the numbers with one pale finger. Shen Wujiu sat beside me, his own column already half empty.
budget:0.cnHint: 师父展示能量____卷轴，提醒我们修炼的代价是有限的。
budget:0.hook: My column showed a number I did not recognise.
budget:0.line: 'Guard your *budget* well, or you will fall before the peak,' said Master Qingwu.

grant:0.en: Xiaoxing knelt on the cold stone floor, both hands raised. She was asking Master Qingwu to allow her entry into the sealed word-garden. 'I *grant* you one hour,' the Master said, pressing a jade token into her small palm. The token glowed, and the iron door at the far wall began to breathe.
grant:0.cnHint: 小星请求师父____她进入封印词园的资格，终于获得了许可。
grant:0.hook: The door opened, and something inside whispered her name.
grant:0.line: 'I *grant* this only because your heart is steady,' said Master Qingwu.

hospital:0.en: The inner healing chamber of Cloud Sea Sect was what outsiders might call a *hospital* — rows of resting mats, shelves of remedy-words, and the faint smell of pine smoke. Shen Wujiu lay on the nearest mat, his breathing slow. I pressed a warm leaf-formula to his wrist and waited for the colour to return to his face.
hospital:0.cnHint: 我在门派的____内守护受伤的师兄，用草药字符为他疗伤。
hospital:0.hook: His eyes opened, but he spoke in a language none of us knew.
hospital:0.line: 'This *hospital* has healed a hundred disciples — it will heal me too,' Shen Wujiu said softly.

island:0.en: On the great map hung above the inner hall door, every floating mountain was marked like an *island* rising from a white sea of cloud. Master Qingwu pointed to the smallest mark near the eastern edge. 'That is where the lost formula was last seen,' she said. The parchment was old, but the ink on that tiny shape was still bright red.
island:0.cnHint: 师父在内堂地图上指出那座孤立的浮山，像云海中的____，那里藏着失传的字符。
island:0.hook: The red ink moved — just once, just slightly.
island:0.line: 'That *island* holds the word that can open the highest gate,' said Master Qingwu.

native:0.en: Xiaoxing touched the oldest herb on the inner shelf, a grey-green plant with no jar. 'This one is *native* to Cloud Sea Peak,' she told me, meaning it had grown here long before the Sect was built, rooted in the rock itself. Its leaves carried a word no master had ever written down, because no brush could hold it.
native:0.cnHint: 小星向我介绍那株____于云海峰的古老草药，它承载着无法书写的字符。
native:0.hook: When she touched it again, the word appeared on her palm.
native:0.line: 'Only a *native* plant of this peak can carry that kind of power,' Xiaoxing said.

tradition:0.en: Before any disciple could enter the word-garden, there was a *tradition* — they must recite the founding oath of the Sect while holding a single lit candle. I stood in the inner hall, flame trembling in my cupped hands, and spoke each line as Shen Wujiu had taught me. The candle did not go out. I had passed.
tradition:0.cnHint: 按照门派____，弟子须持烛诵誓才能进入词园，我屏住呼吸完成了这一仪式。
tradition:0.hook: The candle flame bent toward the sealed door, not toward me.
tradition:0.line: 'Our *tradition* is old, but it has never failed a true heart,' said Shen Wujiu.

africa:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a map so wide it covered the whole inner table. She tapped a mark near the far southern edge — a region the old scrolls called *Africa* — where, she said, another sect had once grown word-herbs in red clay soil under a sun that never dimmed. Their formulas had reached Cloud Sea Peak by way of a single wandering crane.
africa:0.cnHint: 师父展开古地图，指向远方被称为____的土地，那里的字符草药曾随仙鹤传入云海宗。
africa:0.hook: The crane in the courtyard painting slowly turned its painted head.
africa:0.line: 'The words from *Africa* are older than any formula we know,' said Master Qingwu.

confirm:0.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled the assignment scroll on the low desk. My name was brushed in blue ink beside the word 'Ascent.' 'You must *confirm* your acceptance before dawn,' he said quietly, 'or the slot passes to another.' I pressed my palm to the seal. The ink warmed and turned gold.
confirm:0.cnHint: 师兄要求我在天亮前____自己愿意接受飞升任务，否则机会将让给别人。
confirm:0.hook: The moment the ink cooled, a sound rose from deep below the mountain.
confirm:0.line: '*Confirm* your choice now — the scroll does not wait for second thoughts.'

context:0.en: I found the old verse carved above the archive door but could not grasp its meaning alone. Xiaoxing handed me a companion tablet. 'Read it in *context*,' she said, 'with the cloud-chant beside it.' Together the two texts opened like a window. A map of the upper sky appeared in my mind.
context:0.cnHint: 师妹提醒我要结合____来理解门楣上的古老词句，两段文字合在一起才有意义。
context:0.hook: One symbol on the map had no name — only a shape that looked like a door.
context:0.line: 'Without *context*, even the truest word is just an empty sound.'

date:0.en: The Ascent Ceremony had no fixed year — only a condition. Master Qingwu pointed to the stone calendar on the inner wall. 'The *date* is written not in numbers but in cloud-signs,' she said. 'When the third sign appears, we rise.' I traced the carved signs with one finger and felt a faint pulse.
date:0.cnHint: 师尊解释说飞升仪式的____不是用数字记录的，而是由云中征兆来决定。
date:0.hook: That night, the first of the three signs lit up on its own.
date:0.line: 'Mark this *date* in your heart — the clouds will not announce it twice.'

flexible:0.en: The training room was bare except for a single word-rope hanging from the ceiling. 'A rigid formula snaps under pressure,' Master Qingwu said. 'You must be *flexible* — bend the word to the moment.' I reached for the rope and let my breath guide the syllables. The rope curved, lifted, and held my weight.
flexible:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，运用词法时必须保持____，生硬的咒文在压力下会断裂。
flexible:0.hook: At the peak of the hold, the rope whispered something back to me.
flexible:0.line: 'Stay *flexible* in thought, or the word will break before you do.'

fly:0.en: The lesson was simple: speak the word, leave the floor. I had watched Shen Wujiu *fly* a dozen times, but my own attempts had only raised dust. Today something shifted. The syllable left my mouth clean and sure. The floor fell away. Below me the sea of clouds caught the morning light like spilled silver.
fly:0.cnHint: 我终于像师兄一样____了起来，脚下云海在晨光中泛着银色光芒。
fly:0.hook: Then a dark shape rose through the clouds, far larger than any sect bird.
fly:0.line: 'The first time you *fly* alone, the sky remembers your name.'

judge:0.en: At the inner trial, three elders sat behind a low table. Their task was to *judge* which word-formula I had truly mastered and which I had only memorised. I spoke each one slowly. One elder closed her eyes. When she opened them, she placed a white stone before me. That meant: genuine understanding.
judge:0.cnHint: 三位长老坐堂____我究竟真正掌握了哪些词法，而不仅仅是死记硬背。
judge:0.hook: The last elder set down no stone — only looked at the window with uneasy eyes.
judge:0.line: 'We do not *judge* your effort — only what the word does when you release it.'

childhood:0.en: Inside the archive hall, I dusted off a jade scroll older than memory. Master Qingwu touched its edge and grew still. 'These are glyphs from my own *childhood*,' she said softly, 'written when words still felt like wonder rather than weapons.' The candle between us wavered without any wind.
childhood:0.cnHint: 师尊在档案殿中发现了一卷来自她____时期的古老玉简。
childhood:0.hook: The candle's smoke curled into a shape no one had drawn.
childhood:0.line: 'My *childhood* words are still alive inside this scroll.'

equal:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread two portions of silver-leaf herbs across the preparation table, measuring each with a brass weight. 'Every formula demands *equal* parts,' he told me, 'because the art does not forgive a careless hand.' He set down the weight, and both pans held perfectly still, yet the air felt unbalanced.
equal:0.cnHint: 师兄在药台上称量草药，强调配方中每份必须____。
equal:0.hook: One pan sank a hair's width, though nothing had been added.
equal:0.line: 'The formula only works when both parts are *equal*.'

inspire:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a map of the upper peaks inside the study and traced each route with one slow finger. 'Let these paths *inspire* you,' she said, 'not instruct you.' I stared at a peak with no marked trail and felt something open inside my chest like a window meeting morning air.
inspire:0.cnHint: 师尊展开山峰图，希望地图能____弟子找到自己的路。
inspire:0.hook: The unmarked peak seemed to glow faintly on the old map.
inspire:0.line: 'Let the old masters *inspire* you, but do not merely copy them.'

narrow:0.en: The inner library held a *narrow* corridor lined with sealed jars, each containing a single preserved word. I walked it sideways, shoulders brushing both walls, breathing carefully. Shen Wujiu had warned me that opening any jar without permission could release a sound capable of cracking stone. I kept my hands close.
narrow:0.cnHint: 内藏阁中有一条____的走廊，两侧陈列着封存文字的罐子。
narrow:0.hook: One jar hummed softly as I passed, though it had no seal.
narrow:0.line: 'This *narrow* path is the only way to the sealed archive.'

quantity:0.en: Xiaoxing counted the remaining sun-root herbs three times before reporting to Master Qingwu. 'The *quantity* is not enough for every disciple,' she said quietly, setting the basket down with unusual care. Master Qingwu did not answer at once. Outside the herb room window, clouds were rising faster than the hour allowed.
quantity:0.cnHint: 师妹清点草药后发现，剩余的____不够所有弟子使用。
quantity:0.hook: The clouds outside rose as if the mountain itself was breathing.
quantity:0.line: 'The *quantity* of sun-root left will not carry us through the week.'

sustainable:0.en: I asked Master Qingwu whether our sect's method of harvesting cloud-moss could continue for many years. She set down her brush and considered the question longer than I expected. 'Only a *sustainable* practice deserves to be called a path,' she said at last. Rain began to tap the roof in slow, even beats.
sustainable:0.cnHint: 弟子询问师尊，云苔的采集方式是否是____的，能否长久延续。
sustainable:0.hook: The rain's rhythm sounded almost like a warning being spelled out.
sustainable:0.line: 'A practice that exhausts the mountain is never *sustainable*.'

delay:0.en: The morning reading was set for the first bell, but a thick fog had settled inside the hall itself, dimming every word-lamp to a pale smear. Shen Wujiu looked at the clouded lamps and said we should *delay* the recitation until the air cleared. Master Qingwu shook her head slowly and lit one lamp herself.
delay:0.cnHint: 大雾弥漫使晨读无法按时开始，师兄提议____仪式。
delay:0.hook: Master Qingwu's lamp burned clear while every other flame stayed dim.
delay:0.line: 'We must *delay* the reading; the fog has swallowed the words.'

identity:0.en: A sealed letter arrived at the sect hall addressed only to 'the one who hears stone.' No disciple claimed it. Xiaoxing held it up to the word-lamp and whispered that perhaps its true *identity* was a test rather than a message. Master Qingwu lifted the letter without opening it and placed it at the altar.
identity:0.cnHint: 一封神秘来信让众人猜测，师尊将信放上祭坛，未透露收信人的____。
identity:0.hook: The letter's seal glowed once, then faded before anyone could read it.
identity:0.line: 'Until we know its *identity*, this letter belongs to no one hand.'

passion:0.en: Master Qingwu set a single candle on the stone table and told us to speak one word we truly loved. Xiaoxing whispered 'rain.' Shen Wujiu said nothing. I chose 'rise.' Master Qingwu nodded slowly. 'A word spoken with *passion*,' she said, 'carries warmth the clouds can feel.' The candle flame bent, though no wind moved.
passion:0.cnHint: 师尊说，带着____说出的字，连云海都能感受到它的温度。
passion:0.hook: The candle bent again — toward me, and only me.
passion:0.line: 'A word spoken with *passion* can move the clouds themselves.'

temperature:0.en: The inner hall held a row of small jade bowls, each filled with still water. Master Qingwu asked us to write the word 'calm' above each bowl in turn. Where my brushstroke was rushed, the water stayed cold. Where I breathed slowly and wrote with care, the *temperature* of the water rose just enough to send a thin curl of steam into the air.
temperature:0.cnHint: 我写下'静'字时，碗中水的____悄悄上升，冒出一缕白雾。
temperature:0.hook: The last bowl began to tremble before I even raised my brush.
temperature:0.line: 'Watch the *temperature* — it tells you if your word holds true.'

board:0.en: Along the east wall of the study hung a long wooden *board*, its surface carved with every word a disciple must master before the first ascent. Shen Wujiu had already marked seven in faint ink. I counted mine: two. Xiaoxing stood beside me and said nothing, but her sleeve brushed mine like a small, quiet comfort.
board:0.cnHint: 东墙上那块____刻着所有升天前必须掌握的字，师兄已标记了七个。
board:0.hook: One word on the board glowed red in the dark, and it was not one I had studied.
board:0.line: 'Every word on this *board* was paid for with someone's sweat.'

handle:0.en: Master Qingwu placed an old brush before me. Its *handle* was worn smooth by a hundred years of use, the wood the colour of deep water. 'Write the word for wind,' she said. I lifted it, and my fingers found a warmth already waiting there, as if the brush remembered every gust ever set free by the hands before mine.
handle:0.cnHint: 师尊递给我一支古老的笔，笔____因百年使用已磨得光滑温润。
handle:0.hook: As I set the brush down, the window flew open on its own.
handle:0.line: 'Feel the *handle* — it holds the memory of every master who came before.'

ideal:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread four scrolls on the floor and asked which word I thought was most *ideal* for a new disciple to learn first. I studied them: 'still,' 'rise,' 'open,' 'endure.' The hall was quiet. Outside, the clouds shifted. I reached for 'endure,' and Shen Wujiu smiled for the first time since I had arrived.
ideal:0.cnHint: 师兄问我，哪个字是新弟子最____的起点，我伸手选了'忍'。
ideal:0.hook: The scroll I did not choose rolled shut by itself.
ideal:0.line: 'For a first word, 'endure' is *ideal* — it holds all the others inside it.'

ride:0.en: We were not yet allowed on the great cloud-birds, but Master Qingwu said a true disciple could *ride* a single well-chosen word just as far. She wrote 'carry' on a strip of paper, folded it once, and released it. It crossed the entire study before settling softly on the highest shelf, light as a feather.
ride:0.cnHint: 师尊说，弟子能____一个选得好的字，走得不比乘云鸟更近。
ride:0.hook: The strip of paper on the high shelf began, very slowly, to fold itself again.
ride:0.line: 'Learn to *ride* a word well before you ever ask a cloud to carry you.'

adjust:0.en: My first attempt at the word 'rise' pushed too much force into the downstroke. The ink split. Shen Wujiu watched without speaking, then tapped the page twice. 'You must *adjust* the pressure as you move,' he said, 'the way a bird shifts its wings in wind.' I tried again. This time the word stood straight and the ink held.
adjust:0.cnHint: 师兄说我运笔时需要____力度，就像鸟儿在风中调整翅膀。
adjust:0.hook: The straight word hummed once, low and clear, then went still.
adjust:0.line: '*Adjust* the pressure mid-stroke — a rigid word cannot rise.'

basis:0.en: Before the lamps were lit, Master Qingwu gathered us and said that every great formula rested on one simple character learned perfectly. 'That first word is the *basis* of all that follows,' she told us, her voice as even as still water. 'Master it poorly and your tower will lean.' Somewhere in the mountain, a low bell rang without being struck.
basis:0.cnHint: 师尊说，第一个字是所有法诀的____，学得不牢，日后的一切都会倾斜。
basis:0.hook: The bell rang a second time, and no one could find where the sound came from.
basis:0.line: 'One word, mastered truly, is the *basis* of every formula you will ever speak.'

comfortable:0.en: The study hall smelled of old ink and dried herbs. I spread my sleeping mat near the warm stone wall and pulled a thick *comfortable* over my shoulders. Outside, snow pressed against the paper windows. Master Qingwu had said the word for warmth must be learned before the word for fire. I was beginning to understand why. Then the candle flame bent sideways — toward the sealed door.
comfortable:0.cnHint: 我在书室里铺好铺盖，准备好好温习功课，烛火却无端朝封闭的门弯去。
comfortable:0.hook: No wind had entered the room all night.
comfortable:0.line: 'Wrap yourself in something *comfortable* before you open any of those scrolls.'

conclusion:0.en: I had spent three hours comparing the root-words on the library shelf. Shen Wujiu watched me in silence as I set the last scroll down. My *conclusion* was simple: every healing word shared the same opening stroke, like a hand pressed to a wound. He nodded slowly. 'Now write it.' I reached for the brush — and the ink rose to meet my fingers on its own.
conclusion:0.cnHint: 我研读完所有卷轴，得出了一个关于治愈字根的____，但落笔时墨汁竟自己动了。
conclusion:0.hook: Ink does not move unless a word is already alive.
conclusion:0.line: 'Your *conclusion* is correct — but the strokes must come in the right order.'

formal:0.en: It was my first *formal* lesson inside the inner hall. Master Qingwu wore her full grey robe and stood at the high desk without a smile. Each word she spoke landed in my chest like a stone dropped into still water. Xiaoxing sat three seats ahead of me, her brush never stopping. I copied every character twice. At the end, a single dried petal fell from the ceiling with no wind to carry it.
formal:0.cnHint: 我第一次在内堂接受____课，师尊一语落下皆有分量，一片花瓣无风飘落。
formal:0.hook: The petal was from a flower that had not bloomed in years.
formal:0.line: 'This is a *formal* ceremony — hold your brush at the correct height and do not look away.'

happiness:0.en: Xiaoxing had just mastered the word for 'light.' She laughed softly and the lamp above us blazed twice as bright. I felt a quiet *happiness* spreading through my ribs like warm tea — her joy was proof that the words were real, that the path ahead was possible. Master Qingwu said nothing, only turned the page. Then the light in the lamp shifted from gold to a pale, uncertain blue.
happiness:0.cnHint: 小星习得了'光'字，我心中涌起一阵____，然而灯光忽然变成了冷冷的蓝色。
happiness:0.hook: Blue flame in this sect means something has taken notice.
happiness:0.line: 'True *happiness* in this hall comes only after the third reading, never before.'

intelligent:0.en: Shen Wujiu was known as the most *intelligent* disciple in the outer court — he could read a new word once and speak it without error. Yet tonight he sat beside me in the archive room, stuck on a single character, turning the scroll over and over. I offered him my notes. He accepted without pride. A moth landed on the page between us and did not move.
intelligent:0.cnHint: 师兄聪颖过人，却在档案室里对一个字苦思不解，一只飞蛾落在我们之间的纸上一动不动。
intelligent:0.hook: The moth's wings bore the exact shape of the character he sought.
intelligent:0.line: 'An *intelligent* reader knows when to stop and ask — even I had to learn that.'

novel:0.en: The technique Master Qingwu showed us today was entirely *novel*: instead of writing a word, you breathed it. No brush, no ink, only a slow breath shaped into meaning. I felt the syllable form in my throat like a seed. The window misted. Xiaoxing pressed her sleeve to her mouth, wide-eyed. When the mist cleared, a single green shoot had pushed through the stone floor.
novel:0.cnHint: 师尊展示了一种____的修炼法——用呼吸代替笔墨，窗上凝雾，石地上破土而出一株嫩芽。
novel:0.hook: Stone does not crack for ordinary breath.
novel:0.line: 'This method may seem *novel*, but every elder here learned it before they learned the brush.'

political:0.en: Shen Wujiu lowered his voice when he told me this: the choice of which words a disciple learned first was not only a matter of skill. There were *political* reasons too — some families paid to keep certain words off the beginner scrolls. I stared at my copy of the first-year list. Three words had been crossed out in faint grey ink, as if they had never been there. The crossed lines glowed faintly when the fire died down.
political:0.cnHint: 师兄悄悄告诉我，修炼词目的编排背后有____考量，入门卷轴上有几个字被淡淡划去。
political:0.hook: Erased words never stay erased in the Cloud Sea Sect.
political:0.line: 'The order of the scrolls is *political* — do not assume what is listed first is most important.'

property:0.en: Every word learned here became the disciple's *property* — that was the law of the sect, older than the mountain itself. No elder could take it back, no rival could copy it without the original speaker's breath. I wrote my first five words onto a small tile and felt them settle into my bones like stones sinking through water. Then I noticed the tile was warm. Warmer than it should have been.
property:0.cnHint: 宗门规定，弟子习得的字词是其私有____，我将五个字刻入瓦片后，瓦片却散发出异常的热度。
property:0.hook: A tile only grows warm when someone else tries to claim what is yours.
property:0.line: 'Each word is your *property* — guard it the same way you would guard your breath.'

relative:0.en: Inside the medicine hall, Master Qingwu spread two scrolls side by side. 'Cold-root herb and flame-petal herb,' she said. 'Neither is strong alone. Their power is *relative* — each rises only when placed beside its opposite.' I pressed my palm to both scrolls and felt a faint warmth travel up my arm.
relative:0.cnHint: 师尊在药殿中向我展示两种灵草的____关系，我触碰书卷时感到异样的温热。
relative:0.hook: The warmth reached my shoulder and would not stop.
relative:0.line: 'Their power is *relative* — cold means nothing without flame beside it.'

rent:0.en: Shen Wujiu led me to the inner archive, where senior disciples stored their personal formula books on carved wooden shelves. 'Each shelf costs one spirit stone per moon as *rent*,' he said quietly, sliding a slim volume into an empty slot. A draft moved through the sealed room though no window was open.
rent:0.cnHint: 师兄带我去内库，说明存放功法书籍的书架需缴纳____，此时密室中却无故起风。
rent:0.hook: The candle flames all bent toward the same dark corner.
rent:0.line: 'One spirit stone per moon is the *rent* — do not fall behind.'

round:0.en: Master Qingwu set seven small herb jars in a circle on the stone table. 'Each *round* of refinement removes one layer of impurity,' she explained, lifting the first jar. The liquid inside glowed amber, then green, then a pale silver I had never seen before. Outside, a bell rang once and went silent.
round:0.cnHint: 师尊用七只药罐演示炼化的每个____如何去除一层杂质，窗外忽然响起一声孤钟。
round:0.hook: The seventh jar stayed dark, refusing to glow at all.
round:0.line: 'Each *round* clears one veil — seven veils, seven chances to fail.'

structure:0.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled a large diagram across the floor of the study. It showed the *structure* of a cloud-root formation — every channel, every knot, every hollow where qi could gather or leak. 'Memorise this before dawn,' he said, and left the lamp burning low. Shadows moved across the diagram like water.
structure:0.cnHint: 师兄展开一张图，让我在天亮前记住云根阵的____，图上的阴影却像流水般移动。
structure:0.hook: One channel on the diagram had been crossed out in red.
structure:0.line: 'Know the *structure* by heart, or the formation will turn against you.'

typical:0.en: I asked Xiaoxing what a *typical* morning in the Cloud Sea Sect looked like before I arrived. She smiled and said, 'Dew collection, two hours of reading, one hour of silence.' She handed me a bowl of warm grain. At the bottom of the bowl, pressed into the clay, was a symbol I could not name.
typical:0.cnHint: 晓星向我描述加入之前门派____的清晨作息，我在碗底发现了一个陌生符文。
typical:0.hook: The symbol pulsed once, faint as a heartbeat, then was still.
typical:0.line: 'That is a *typical* morning here — simple, until it is not.'

vacation:0.en: Shen Wujiu told me that once every three years the sect grants disciples a *vacation* of seven days. During those days the library seals itself and the training grounds go quiet. 'Some disciples use the time to travel below the clouds,' he said softly. He did not say what they found when they returned.
vacation:0.cnHint: 师兄说门派每三年会给弟子放一次____，图书馆会自动封闭，他轻声说有人下云游历。
vacation:0.hook: He looked at his own hands as if they belonged to someone else.
vacation:0.line: 'Seven days of *vacation* — but the sect never forgets what you do with them.'

acquire:0.en: Master Qingwu placed a single dried leaf on my palm. 'You cannot be taught to sense qi,' she said. 'You must *acquire* that feeling yourself, the way roots acquire water — slowly, without force.' I closed my eyes. The leaf grew warm, then cool, then warm again. I did not know which I had caused.
acquire:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我感知灵气的能力必须靠自己____，就像树根吸水，我闭眼感应那片叶子。
acquire:0.hook: When I opened my eyes, the leaf had turned to ash.
acquire:0.line: 'You must *acquire* it yourself — no master can hand you that feeling.'

adequate:0.en: Xiaoxing reviewed my first spirit-formula inscription and set it down without praise or blame. 'The strokes are *adequate*,' she said carefully. 'They will hold — for now.' She tapped the final character, which had a hairline crack running through its centre that I had not noticed until that moment.
adequate:0.cnHint: 晓星审阅我第一张灵符后说笔法____，我这才注意到最后一个字有一道细微的裂纹。
adequate:0.hook: A crack in a spirit-formula grows, given time and pressure.
adequate:0.line: '*Adequate* means it will hold — it does not mean it will hold long.'

attribute:0.en: Master Qingwu placed a single white feather on the stone table before me. 'Every disciple who rises to the upper peaks carries one *attribute* that sets them apart,' she said quietly. 'Yours is not yet clear to me.' The feather trembled, though no wind stirred in the room.
attribute:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，每位能飞升的弟子都有一项独特的____，但我的尚不明朗。
attribute:0.hook: The feather rose one inch, then fell completely still.
attribute:0.line: 'An *attribute* unseen is a flame unlit — find it before the trial comes.'

badly:0.en: I had practiced the Rising Script three hundred times, yet the characters still scattered like frightened birds whenever I tried to hold them in my mind. My hands shook *badly* as I unrolled the fourth attempt before Shen Wujiu, who watched without a word. Ink pooled at the edges of the silk like a dark omen.
badly:0.cnHint: 我的双手____地颤抖着，第四次尝试写出飞升文字时依然失败。
badly:0.hook: Shen Wujiu picked up the silk and turned it slowly upside down.
badly:0.line: 'You want this *badly* enough — that hunger is the only thing keeping the script from burning the room.'

bridge:0.en: Deep inside the Sect's archive room, a narrow shelf of stone served as a *bridge* between two towering walls of sealed jars, each jar holding a sleeping word-spirit. Xiaoxing crossed it without looking down. I followed, counting each step, aware that one wrong move would shatter a century of gathered knowledge.
bridge:0.cnHint: 档案室里，一道窄石台____着两面装满封印词灵的高墙，我小心翼翼地跟着师妹走过。
bridge:0.hook: One jar at the far end began to hum all on its own.
bridge:0.line: 'This *bridge* has held for a hundred years — walk with respect, not with fear.'

casual:0.en: Shen Wujiu leaned against the window frame with a *casual* ease that made my own stiffness feel foolish. He was reviewing the Ascension Charts as though they were nothing more than a list of daily chores. Yet I noticed his eyes did not blink once in the time I stood watching him.
casual:0.cnHint: 师兄以一种____的姿态靠在窗边翻阅飞升图谱，但他的眼睛始终一眨不眨。
casual:0.hook: He closed the chart and said, 'You have been standing there too long.'
casual:0.line: 'Do not mistake my *casual* manner — I have read these charts every night for three years.'

closely:0.en: Master Qingwu held the lamp *closely* to the wall where the old ascension record was carved, tracing each stroke with one careful finger. Xiaoxing and I pressed near, barely breathing. The names of those who had risen were deep and clear; the names of those who had failed were worn almost to nothing.
closely:0.cnHint: 师尊把灯____地靠近石壁，照亮了飞升记录中那些几乎磨损殆尽的名字。
closely:0.hook: One name at the very bottom still bled faint red pigment.
closely:0.line: 'Look *closely* at what is almost gone — the faded names teach more than the bright ones.'

commit:0.en: Before the inner door of the archive could be opened, each disciple had to press a hand to the seal-stone and *commit* to returning every word-spirit undisturbed. I pressed my palm flat against the cold surface. The stone warmed under my hand and then pulsed once, like a slow heartbeat accepting a promise.
commit:0.cnHint: 进入档案内室前，每位弟子必须触碰封印石，____于归还所有词灵。
commit:0.hook: The stone pulsed a second time, which was not supposed to happen.
commit:0.line: 'To *commit* to this place means you carry its silence with you when you leave.'

concentrate:0.en: 'Still your breath and *concentrate*,' Master Qingwu said, standing at the far side of the preparation room. 'The ascension current is thin tonight; if your thoughts scatter, it will pass through you without catching.' I closed my eyes and gathered every thread of attention I had, the way one gathers water in cupped hands.
concentrate:0.cnHint: 师尊命我____精神，因为今夜飞升气流极细，心神一散便会错过。
concentrate:0.hook: A sound like distant wind filled the room, then went completely silent.
concentrate:0.line: '*Concentrate* as if each breath were the last drop of water in a dry summer.'

conscious:0.en: The preparation room grew cold. I became deeply *conscious* of the seams between the floor stones, of the ink drying on my sleeve, of the exact distance between my feet and the chalk circle drawn at the room's centre. Xiaoxing later told me that this sharpened awareness was itself the first true sign of readiness to rise.
conscious:0.cnHint: 室内变冷，我开始____地感受到周围每一处细节，师妹说这正是飞升准备好的第一个征兆。
conscious:0.hook: The chalk circle glowed once, faint gold, and then went dark.
conscious:0.line: 'Be *conscious* of every small thing around you — the current reads your attention before it lifts you.'

obvious:0.en: Inside the Sutra Hall, rows of jade slips glowed with pale light. I reached for a basic formula, but Master Qingwu stopped my hand. 'Look again,' she said softly. The crack running through its core was *obvious* once she pointed — a flaw that would have sent my qi spiralling out of control.
obvious:0.cnHint: 师尊提醒我，玉简上有一道____的裂纹，不可轻取。
obvious:0.hook: A flawed slip in the wrong hands could shatter the entire hall.
obvious:0.line: 'The danger is *obvious* — a cracked slip will break your qi path.'

ordinary:0.en: The preparation room smelled of pine ash and old silk. Shen Wujiu handed me a small grey pill, plain as a river stone. 'Do not mistake it,' he warned. No *ordinary* herb could survive being ground with cloud-frost powder, yet this one had — and now it hummed with quiet, dangerous life.
ordinary:0.cnHint: 师兄递给我一粒外表____的丹药，但它暗藏惊人的力量。
ordinary:0.hook: Something that small should not have a heartbeat.
ordinary:0.line: 'This is no *ordinary* pill — treat it with great care.'

pace:0.en: Before the Ascension Trial, I could not keep still. I began to *pace* the length of my small chamber, counting the stone tiles, steadying my breath. Xiaoxing stood in the doorway, watching me without a word. On my seventh pass she placed a warm cup of pine-needle tea into my restless hands.
pace:0.cnHint: 考验前我在室内____，小星悄悄端来一杯茶安抚我。
pace:0.hook: The tea tasted faintly of lightning — and something else entirely.
pace:0.line: 'Stop — *pacing* will only scatter your inner wind.'

participate:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled the trial roster on the long cedar table. Every senior disciple's name was brushed in red. Mine was not. 'Only those who have sealed their third gate may *participate*,' she said, eyes steady on my face. I pressed my palm to my chest and felt — faintly, unmistakably — the third gate stir.
participate:0.cnHint: 师尊说，只有封印第三道关的弟子才能____此次飞升试炼。
participate:0.hook: The gate stirred once, then fell terrifyingly silent.
participate:0.line: 'You may *participate* — if your third gate answers by dawn.'

pilot:0.en: High on the inner wall hung a portrait: a woman in white standing at the prow of a cloud-skiff, hands loose at her sides. 'She was the sect's first *pilot*,' Shen Wujiu said, voice low with respect. 'She steered a dying skiff through a storm of broken qi and brought every disciple home.'
pilot:0.cnHint: 师兄向我介绍壁画中那位驾驭云舟的____，她曾在风暴中救下所有弟子。
pilot:0.hook: The painted woman's eyes seemed to follow us to the door.
pilot:0.line: 'A true *pilot* feels the wind before it moves.'

primary:0.en: Master Qingwu laid three jade slips on the desk: one for breath control, one for qi flow, one for word-sealing. 'The *primary* lesson is the first,' she said, tapping it. 'Without breath, the other two are empty shells.' I had spent weeks on the harder slips. I picked up the first one, ashamed.
primary:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，三块玉简中____的那块是调息之法，我却一直忽视它。
primary:0.hook: The simplest slip grew burning-hot the moment I touched it.
primary:0.line: 'Breath control is the *primary* root — neglect it and you fall.'

priority:0.en: The night before the trial, Xiaoxing spread her notes across the floor of my room and pointed to a single line circled in red ink. 'This seal is your *priority*,' she said firmly. 'Master Qingwu circled it herself. Learn it before dawn or the ascension wind will pass you by entirely.'
priority:0.cnHint: 小星告诉我，师尊亲自圈出的那道符印是明天试炼前的____。
priority:0.hook: Dawn, she said — but outside the window, the sky was already pale.
priority:0.line: 'Your *priority* tonight is this one seal — nothing else matters.'

throughout:0.en: The candle in my chamber burned *throughout* the long night as I studied the ascension formula, stroke by stroke. Voices of other disciples rose and faded in the corridor outside. By the time silence settled, the candle had burned to its base and the formula glowed — steady and complete — behind my closed eyes.
throughout:0.cnHint: 整整一夜，我的烛火____长夜，直到飞升心法在脑海中清晰成形。
throughout:0.hook: The burnt-out candle left a spiral of smoke shaped like a gate.
throughout:0.line: 'You burned your light *throughout* the dark — the sect is proud.'

worldwide:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled an ancient map across the stone table. Every floating mountain known to the sect was marked in fading ink. 'Our order once spread *worldwide*,' she said softly, tracing a chain of peaks that stretched beyond the sea of clouds. I studied the marks and felt the weight of what we were meant to restore.
worldwide:0.cnHint: 师尊展开古地图，讲述云海宗的势力曾____遍布，我深感责任之重。
worldwide:0.hook: One peak on the map was circled in fresh red ink.
worldwide:0.line: 'Our healing words were once *worldwide*, carried on every wind.'

accomplish:0.en: Shen Wujiu set a small jade jar on my desk before dawn. Inside was a single dried syllable-herb, its glow faint but steady. 'To *accomplish* even one true healing word,' he said, 'you must first sit with it until you hear it breathe.' I placed my palm over the jar and listened to the silence between my own heartbeats.
accomplish:0.cnHint: 师兄告诫我，要____一个真正的治愈词，需先静心感受它的气息。
accomplish:0.hook: The herb pulsed once, and the candle flame bent toward it.
accomplish:0.line: 'Few disciples ever *accomplish* the first listening before the third moon.'

address:0.en: Master Qingwu gathered us in the inner hall to *address* a matter no elder had raised in years: a word had gone silent. Somewhere in the library, a healing formula had stopped glowing. Her voice stayed calm, but her hands, folded at her sleeves, were very still. I noticed Xiaoxing press her fingers together under her robe.
address:0.cnHint: 师尊在内堂____了一件多年未提的事：一个治愈词的光芒已经熄灭。
address:0.hook: From deep in the library came a sound like paper tearing itself.
address:0.line: 'I must *address* this now, before the silence spreads further.'

barely:0.en: The first formula Shen Wujiu taught me was only four syllables long, yet I could *barely* hold its shape in my mind. Each time I reached the final sound, the first one slipped away like mist. He did not seem surprised. He handed me a brush and said nothing. Outside the window, clouds drifted past the mountain's root, unhurried and vast.
barely:0.cnHint: 师兄教我第一个四音节咒式，我____能在脑中维持它的形态，反复失败。
barely:0.hook: At midnight the brush moved on its own, tracing a fifth syllable.
barely:0.line: 'I could *barely* name the wind-word when I first stood where you stand.'

blame:0.en: A jar of sound-sealed herbs had cracked overnight, spilling its light across the floor of the preparation room. No one admitted to leaving it near the window. Master Qingwu looked at each of us in turn. 'The *blame* matters less than the repair,' she said at last, kneeling to gather the scattered glow with steady hands. I felt the lesson land before she spoke another word.
blame:0.cnHint: 储药房的封音药罐破裂，师尊说比起追究____，修复更为重要。
blame:0.hook: The spilled light slowly formed the outline of a word none of us recognized.
blame:0.line: 'Do not carry *blame* like a stone — it will pull you below the clouds.'

chat:0.en: Xiaoxing found me sitting alone on the east ledge, watching the cloud sea turn gold at dusk. She sat beside me without asking and began to *chat* about small things: the taste of the morning's herb tea, a bird she had seen flying upward instead of down. I did not say much, but the tightness in my chest eased. When she left, the stars were out, earlier than expected.
chat:0.cnHint: 师妹坐在我身旁，随意地____着琐事，我心中的紧绷感悄悄消散了。
chat:0.hook: One star moved slowly against the rest, tracing the shape of a word.
chat:0.line: 'Let us *chat* here a while — the sky listens well at this hour.'

combat:0.en: The training scroll on my desk described *combat* not as a clash of force but as a conversation between two opposing words. Whoever chose the wiser syllable first would end it before it truly began. Shen Wujiu had underlined one sentence in faint brush strokes: knowing when to stay silent is itself a word. I read it three times before I understood he had left it there for me.
combat:0.cnHint: 训练卷轴将____定义为两个对立词之间的对话，师兄的批注让我深思。
combat:0.hook: A second scroll rolled off the shelf and landed open at a different page.
combat:0.line: 'In true *combat*, the right word spoken first ends everything.'

danger:0.en: Late in the evening, Xiaoxing showed me a section of the inner wall where the carved words had begun to fade. 'This is *danger*,' she said plainly, running one finger along the pale stone without touching the marks. The wall held the oldest sealing formula in the sect hall. If its words dimmed fully, the mountain's root would have nothing left to hold it to the sky.
danger:0.cnHint: 师妹指着内墙上渐渐褪色的封印符文，说这是真正的____。
danger:0.hook: As we watched, one carved stroke thinned to almost nothing.
danger:0.line: 'The real *danger* is not a rival sect — it is forgetting the first word.'

dinner:0.en: The great hall of Cloud Sea Sect glowed with lantern light. Long tables held rare dishes prepared from spirit-grain grown above the clouds. Master Qingwu had called every disciple together for a *dinner* to mark the opening of the Ascension Trial. Steam rose from the bowls like morning mist.
dinner:0.cnHint: 师尊在大殿设____，宣布飞升试炼即将开始。
dinner:0.hook: But one seat at the head table remained coldly empty.
dinner:0.line: 'This *dinner* marks the last meal we share before the trial,' said Master Qingwu.

embrace:0.en: Xiaoxing stood at the edge of the inner hall, arms wrapped around herself as if cold. When I stepped forward and offered a steady hand, she lifted her eyes. She said the trial ahead was vast, too vast to face alone. To *embrace* that vastness, she whispered, one must first find stillness within.
embrace:0.cnHint: 小星说，只有____内心的广阔，才能踏上飞升之路。
embrace:0.hook: Then the lantern above her head flickered and went dark.
embrace:0.line: 'To *embrace* the path, you must first let go of fear,' she said.

explanation:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread the old scroll across the stone table and traced each symbol with one careful finger. I asked why certain herb-words held power while others faded. His *explanation* was quiet but clear: only words grown in sincerity could take root in the air and lift a person higher. I copied every line.
explanation:0.cnHint: 师兄给出____，说明为何有些词句能助人飞升。
explanation:0.hook: One symbol on the scroll pulsed faintly, as if it had heard him.
explanation:0.line: 'My *explanation* is simple — a false word will never carry you upward,' said Shen Wujiu.

intend:0.en: Master Qingwu stood before the candle-lit map of the floating peaks and said nothing for a long moment. I did not *intend* to speak, but the question left my mouth before I could stop it: which peak was chosen for my trial? She turned slowly, her silver sleeves catching the candlelight like wings.
intend:0.cnHint: 我本不____开口，却还是向师尊问出了心中那个问题。
intend:0.hook: Her answer was a single raised finger pointing straight up.
intend:0.line: 'I *intend* to watch each of you face the trial alone,' said Master Qingwu.

leadership:0.en: The inner hall held a carved chair no one had sat in for three years. Shen Wujiu told me that the last senior disciple who held *leadership* of our training circle had vanished the morning after his own Ascension Trial. The chair faced the window. Outside, clouds drifted in slow, patient circles.
leadership:0.cnHint: 师兄提起上一任负责____的师兄，在飞升后消失无踪。
leadership:0.hook: A single feather rested on the carved seat, fresh and white.
leadership:0.line: 'True *leadership* means walking into the unknown first,' said Shen Wujiu.

locate:0.en: The preparation room was filled with jars of dried spirit-herbs, each sealed with a paper tag. I had to *locate* the three herbs whose names, when spoken aloud together, would open the trial gate. My fingers moved jar by jar. Somewhere above the rafters, wind moved through a gap I could not find.
locate:0.cnHint: 我需要在满室药罐中____三味关键灵草。
locate:0.hook: The third jar, when I touched it, was already warm.
locate:0.line: 'Can you *locate* the herb called Sky-Root before the bell rings?' asked Xiaoxing.

original:0.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled what he said was the *original* copy of the Ascension Formula, written by the sect's founder on bark-paper thin as a breath. The newer copies hung on every wall, but this one felt different under my eyes, as if the words still carried the weight of the hand that first formed them.
original:0.cnHint: 师兄展示了飞升诀的____版本，那是开派祖师亲笔所写。
original:0.hook: One word near the bottom had been crossed out in red.
original:0.line: 'The *original* text says something the copies have always left out,' said Shen Wujiu.

overcome:0.en: I sat alone in the reading room, the Ascension Formula open before me. Every disciple before me had failed at the same passage, where the words grew too dense to hold in the mind at once. Master Qingwu had told us that to *overcome* that passage, we must stop forcing it and simply breathe. I breathed.
overcome:0.cnHint: 我独坐书室，试图____飞升诀中那段令人迷茫的难关。
overcome:0.hook: On my third breath, the characters began to softly glow.
overcome:0.line: 'You can only *overcome* the hard passage when you stop fighting it,' said Master Qingwu.

conventional:0.en: Master Qingwu led me through the inner hall, past rows of sealed jars. She paused before a plain stone table. 'Most disciples follow *conventional* methods,' she said, arranging three dried herbs in a triangle. 'But the Cloud Sea Sect was never built on most.' The candle flames all leaned east at once.
conventional:0.cnHint: 师尊向我展示炼药台，说门派从不依赖____的方法。
conventional:0.hook: Every candle in the hall bent toward the same hidden door.
conventional:0.line: 'Most disciples follow *conventional* methods, but you were not sent here to be most.'

disappear:0.en: Shen Wujiu stood before the shelf of practice scrolls, frowning. One scroll, sealed in blue ribbon, had been there that morning. Now the ribbon lay on the empty shelf like a shed skin. 'Texts do not simply *disappear*,' he said softly. I looked at my own hands and felt a cold certainty rise.
disappear:0.cnHint: 师兄发现一卷重要的修炼秘籍____了，留下一段空白。
disappear:0.hook: The ribbon still held the warmth of a living hand.
disappear:0.line: 'Texts do not simply *disappear* — someone carried it out before dawn.'

district:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a wide chart across the reading table. The floating mountains were divided by thin silver lines. 'The eastern *district* of the Cloud Sea holds the oldest herb groves,' she said, pressing her finger to a circle marked in red. 'And the oldest dangers.' Outside, wind moved through the hall like a held breath.
district:0.cnHint: 师尊展开云海地图，指向最古老、也最危险的____。
district:0.hook: The red circle on the map pulsed once, faint as a heartbeat.
district:0.line: 'The eastern *district* is where power grows oldest — and hungriest.'

greatly:0.en: Xiaoxing placed a small jade bowl on the study table and recited the water formula three times. The liquid inside rose, then stilled into a perfect mirror. Shen Wujiu nodded. 'Your focus has *greatly* improved since last moon,' he said. She smiled but kept her eyes on the bowl, where something dark briefly swam.
greatly:0.cnHint: 师兄称赞师妹的专注力____进步，但碗中出现了异象。
greatly:0.hook: In the still water, a shadow moved that had no source.
greatly:0.line: 'Your focus has *greatly* improved — do not let pride cloud what you just saw.'

imitate:0.en: I found Xiaoxing at the inner desk, copying hand signs from a faded diagram pinned to the wall. 'I try to *imitate* the master's form,' she said without turning, 'but my fingers remember a different shape.' She pressed her palms flat on the table. The paper diagram curled at its edges and began to smoke.
imitate:0.cnHint: 师妹努力____师尊的手印，却引发了意想不到的反应。
imitate:0.hook: The diagram burned from the center outward, leaving the border whole.
imitate:0.line: 'I try to *imitate* the master's form, but something in me keeps refusing.'

implement:0.en: Master Qingwu set a narrow bronze *implement* on the reading table between us. It looked like a simple measuring rod, yet it hummed against the wood. 'Every craft needs its proper tool,' she said. 'This one reads the weight of a word before you speak it.' I reached forward, and the rod rolled away on its own.
implement:0.cnHint: 师尊拿出一件青铜____，声称它能感知话语的份量。
implement:0.hook: The bronze rod stopped at the table's edge and pointed at me.
implement:0.line: 'This *implement* will tell you whether your word carries true weight or only air.'

mood:0.en: The study lamps burned lower than usual when I entered the inner chamber. Shen Wujiu sat with his back to the door, neither reading nor moving. 'The mountain is in a strange *mood* tonight,' he said at last. 'I have felt it shift three times since dusk.' Above us, the ceiling beams let out a long, slow groan.
mood:0.cnHint: 师兄察觉到山峰的____异常，已经变换了三次。
mood:0.hook: The fourth shift came then, and the lamps went out together.
mood:0.line: 'When the mountain is in this *mood*, even silence becomes a warning.'

motivation:0.en: Master Qingwu asked me to stand before the wall of names — every disciple who had ever ascended. 'Before you climb further,' she said, 'name your *motivation*.' I opened my mouth, then closed it. The names on the wall seemed to lean in. Whatever I had planned to say felt too small for the room and the hour.
motivation:0.cnHint: 师尊要求我站在名碑前，说出自己修炼的____。
motivation:0.hook: One name on the wall glowed faint gold as I fell silent.
motivation:0.line: 'A true disciple knows their *motivation* before the mountain asks it of them.'

threaten:0.en: Inside the Hall of Scrolls, dark clouds gathered beyond the narrow windows. Master Qingwu set down her brush and spoke without turning. 'These storm-words do not merely warn,' she said. 'They *threaten* every disciple who has not yet sealed their core.' The candles bent as if listening.
threaten:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉弟子们，悬挂在卷轴殿外的风暴并非警示，而是____着每一位尚未封印本源的修者。
threaten:0.hook: The candles went out one by one.

throw:0.en: Shen Wujiu stood at the centre of the training hall, weighing the jade token in his palm. Everyone knew that joining the Ascension Trial was a *throw* — one chance, no return path. He closed his fingers around the token, breathed once, and stepped toward the register.
throw:0.cnHint: 师兄明白，参加飞升试炼是一场____，但他还是握紧令牌走向了名册。
throw:0.hook: The register glowed red the moment his name touched the page.
throw:0.line: 'This *throw* is the only path left to me.'

unlike:0.en: The inner study smelled of pine ash and old silk. Xiaoxing noticed at once that this room was *unlike* any she had entered before — the shelves held no books, only small clay jars sealed with wax, each one humming at a different pitch, as if alive.
unlike:0.cnHint: 小星发现师门内室与她以前见过的任何地方____，架子上全是会发声的泥封罐。
unlike:0.hook: One jar rocked on its shelf, then was still.
unlike:0.line: 'This hall is *unlike* anything I have ever entered before.'

vast:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled the oldest map in the sect's keeping. The chart showed the sky-roots beneath their mountain, spreading outward in a *vast* web that reached every peak above the Cloud Sea. 'We stand,' she said softly, 'on one small knot of an endless thread.'
vast:0.cnHint: 师尊展开古老的山脉图，弟子们看到了延伸至云海之上每座山峰的____网络。
vast:0.hook: At the map's far edge, three peaks were circled in red.
vast:0.line: 'A *vast* web of sky-roots holds every mountain in place.'

absolutely:0.en: Shen Wujiu held the cracked spirit-vessel over the flame to show the others. 'It is *absolutely* empty,' he said, 'not a trace of essence left.' The room fell quiet. Without that vessel, the Ascension Gate could not be opened before the next full moon.
absolutely:0.cnHint: 师兄向大家展示破损的灵器，说它____空了，没有一丝灵气残留，众人沉默了。
absolutely:0.hook: Someone had emptied it — and left the lid warm.
absolutely:0.line: 'The vessel is *absolutely* empty; not one trace remains.'

accumulate:0.en: Each morning Xiaoxing pressed her palms to the cold stone floor of the study and breathed until the room brightened. 'You must *accumulate* stillness before you can move mountains,' Master Qingwu had said. After forty mornings, the floor beneath her hands had turned faintly warm.
accumulate:0.cnHint: 小星每天清晨在书房练习吐纳，因为师尊说只有____了足够的静气，才能撼动山岳。
accumulate:0.hook: On the forty-first morning, the stone cracked.
accumulate:0.line: '*Accumulate* stillness first; only then can you move mountains.'

breakfast:0.en: They were halfway through *breakfast* — warm grain broth and dried herb cakes — when the sect bell rang three long strokes. Master Qingwu set down her bowl without haste. 'Three strokes mean the Archive is open,' she said. 'Leave the meal. Bring your writing brushes.'
breakfast:0.cnHint: 弟子们正在____，宗门的钟声突然敲响了三下，师尊放下碗，让大家放弃饭食立刻带笔出发。
breakfast:0.hook: The Archive had not opened in seven years.
breakfast:0.line: 'Leave *breakfast*; the Archive will not wait for full bowls.'

capacity:0.en: Master Qingwu placed five spirit-stones in a row and asked each disciple to lift them with will alone. None could hold more than three. 'Your *capacity* for essence is fixed today,' she said, 'but the Ascension Trial will demand you carry the weight of all five.' No one spoke.
capacity:0.cnHint: 师尊用五块灵石测试每位弟子的____，所有人都只能托举三块，而飞升试炼要求举起全部。
capacity:0.hook: Shen Wujiu's fifth stone floated — then shattered.
capacity:0.line: 'Your *capacity* today is three; the trial demands five.'

consideration:0.en: Master Qingwu spread eight glowing word-scrolls across the stone table. 'Each one holds a different path to the sky,' she said. After long silence, she chose the scroll marked 'wind.' Every *consideration* she gave to the others left a faint trace of light in the air, as though the rejected words still wished to be chosen.
consideration:0.cnHint: 师尊在挑选飞升法诀时，经过了深思熟虑的____，最终选定了风字卷轴。
consideration:0.hook: The last rejected scroll trembled once, then sealed itself shut forever.
consideration:0.line: 'Every *consideration* matters when the wrong word could unmake the sky.'

disaster:0.en: Xiaoxing mixed the word 'rise' with the word 'stone' by mistake. The formula collapsed inward, and a crack split the practice-room floor from wall to wall. Master Qingwu arrived within moments, pressing one calm hand to the crack to still it. 'This is not yet a *disaster*,' she said quietly, 'but it is a warning carved in the earth itself.'
disaster:0.cnHint: 小星在练习飞升法诀时念错了字，差点酿成一场____，所幸师尊及时赶到。
disaster:0.hook: Beneath the sealed crack, something deep in the mountain gave a slow, low groan.
disaster:0.line: 'A single wrong word is enough to turn progress into *disaster*.'

emergency:0.en: A bell rang three times in the inner hall — the signal Shen Wujiu had taught me to fear. He was at my door before the third ring faded. 'Dress quickly,' he said. 'This is an *emergency*. The cloud-anchor word at the mountain's root is fading, and without it the peak drifts free.' I had never seen his hands shake before that morning.
emergency:0.cnHint: 山根锚字突然衰减，师兄来敲门说这是一场____，必须立刻行动。
emergency:0.hook: Through the window, the horizon tilted — just slightly, just enough to notice.
emergency:0.line: 'Move now — this counts as an *emergency* for the whole mountain.'

familiar:0.en: I entered the archive room and ran my fingers along the old word-jars. The soft hum they gave off was *familiar* to me now — a sound I had heard each morning since joining the Cloud Sea Sect. Yet today one jar hummed a half-step higher than the rest, as though it carried a word that was waking up on its own.
familiar:0.cnHint: 我对存放法字的古旧罐子发出的嗡鸣声已经很____了，但今天有一只罐子的声音变了。
familiar:0.hook: The jar's seal glowed faint gold, a colour it had never shown before.
familiar:0.line: 'The archive should feel *familiar* to you — if it does not, something has changed.'

furthermore:0.en: Master Qingwu wrote the word 'ascend' on the board and asked each of us to copy it. She corrected my brush angle, then my breath. 'The stroke must rise like smoke,' she said. '*Furthermore*, your intent must rise before the brush does, or the word will carry no weight at all.' I copied it again. This time the ink lifted slightly off the page.
furthermore:0.cnHint: 师尊纠正了我的笔法，____还告诉我，意念必须先于笔锋而升。
furthermore:0.hook: The ink that had lifted hung in the air for three full breaths before fading.
furthermore:0.line: '*Furthermore*, a word written without intention is just a mark, not a formula.'

hardly:0.en: I had been studying the flight-word for six days and could *hardly* hold its shape in my mind for more than a breath before it dissolved. Shen Wujiu watched without comment until the seventh attempt, when a small white feather rose from the floor unbidden and floated to the ceiling. 'There,' he said simply. 'That was it.'
hardly:0.cnHint: 我苦练飞升字诀六天，____能在脑中维持住它的形状，直到第七次才有了微小的突破。
hardly:0.hook: The feather stayed at the ceiling long after we both stopped looking at it.
hardly:0.line: 'I could *hardly* believe it the first time I held a word long enough to fly.'

hinder:0.en: The narrow practice room had low beams and stacked jars of dormant words along every wall. Shen Wujiu warned me that clutter could *hinder* the flow of a spoken formula — stray objects catch the sound and pull it sideways. I cleared a path down the center. The next time I spoke the ascent word, my voice moved in a straight line all the way to the window.
hinder:0.cnHint: 师兄提醒我，杂乱的环境会____法诀的气流传导，清理空间后我的练习顺畅多了。
hinder:0.hook: Outside the window, a single cloud stopped moving and held its shape, listening.
hinder:0.line: 'Do not let a cluttered space *hinder* what your voice is trying to do.'

injury:0.en: I pressed the healing-word to my palm where the failed formula had burned it. The skin cooled at once, and the redness faded to nothing. Master Qingwu observed from the doorway. 'An *injury* from your own word is the sharpest teacher,' she said, her tone neither cold nor kind, simply true. Outside, the evening clouds turned the colour of copper, then of ash.
injury:0.cnHint: 我用治愈字诀处理了自己因法诀失败而留下的____，师尊说这是最深刻的教训。
injury:0.hook: The ash-coloured clouds gathered at the window ledge and did not drift away.
injury:0.line: 'Every *injury* a word leaves on you is a lesson it could not teach any other way.'

lift:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old wood and dried spiritual herbs. Master Qingwu stood at the centre, one arm raised. 'Feel the word rise in your chest,' she said. A faint *lift* of warm air followed her voice, as if the hall itself breathed upward, carrying the syllables toward the high ceiling like smoke seeking open sky.
lift:0.cnHint: 师尊在内堂演示如何让词语产生____的力量，连空气都随之上升。
lift:0.hook: A crack split the stone floor, and no one had touched it.
lift:0.line: 'Let the word give you a *lift*, and your feet will forget the ground.'

mainly:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread three scrolls across the low table and tapped the widest one. 'The first-year lessons are *mainly* about listening,' he said. 'You read the word, you hear it inside, you feel its weight.' Outside the window, the mountain hummed softly, as if agreeing with every syllable he spoke.
mainly:0.cnHint: 师兄向我解释，第一年的修炼____是关于倾听词语的内在声音。
mainly:0.hook: Then the scroll rolled itself shut, and Shen Wujiu went very still.
mainly:0.line: 'Our training is *mainly* listening — speak too soon and the word turns cold.'

moral:0.en: Master Qingwu set a small clay jar on the altar stone. 'Every healing word has a *moral*,' she said quietly. 'It will not flow toward a closed heart.' I held my breath. The jar began to glow, faint gold at first, then brighter, as though testing the room before deciding whether to stay.
moral:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，每一个治愈之词都有其____，不会流向封闭的心。
moral:0.hook: The glow died, and the jar felt heavier than any stone I had ever held.
moral:0.line: 'Learn the *moral* of each word before you speak it aloud.'

nor:0.en: Xiaoxing shook her head over my ink-stained notes. 'You have *nor* the right stroke nor the right breath,' she said, not unkindly. She guided my brush back to the top of the page. The word I had been trying to write sat crooked on the paper, leaking a thin thread of pale mist that neither of us could explain.
nor:0.cnHint: 师妹指出我的笔法____对，气息也不对，但她并不严厉。
nor:0.hook: The pale mist curled toward the window and slipped through the wall.
nor:0.line: '*Nor* your stroke nor your breath is steady — start again from stillness.'

pick:0.en: 'You may *pick* one word from the shelf before tonight's lesson ends,' Master Qingwu said, gesturing at the long row of sealed jars. Each jar held a single character glowing like a firefly. My hand moved without thinking toward a jar near the end. The moment my fingers touched the clay, every other jar in the room went dark.
pick:0.cnHint: 师尊允许我从架子上____一个词语，但我的选择让其他所有词罐都熄灭了。
pick:0.hook: Master Qingwu did not look surprised, and that was the most frightening thing.
pick:0.line: '*Pick* carefully — a word you are not ready for will pick you instead.'

pollution:0.en: Shen Wujiu pointed to a grey smear across the corner of my practice scroll. 'That is *pollution*,' he said. 'A word spoken in anger leaves a stain that weakens every word around it.' I looked at the smear. It spread a little as I watched, very slowly, the way frost spreads across cold glass at the edge of dawn.
pollution:0.cnHint: 师兄指出我练习卷上的灰色污迹是词语____，由愤怒中发音所留。
pollution:0.hook: By morning the smear had reached the centre of the scroll.
pollution:0.line: 'Anger in your voice is *pollution* — it dims every word you have ever learned.'

quit:0.en: I had been sitting with the same word for two hours when Xiaoxing appeared at the door. 'Do not *quit* before it answers,' she said softly, settling beside me without being asked. Together we sat in silence. Then the word on the page shifted, just slightly, like a sleeping creature turning toward warmth.
quit:0.cnHint: 当我几乎想放弃时，师妹来到门口，告诉我不要____。
quit:0.hook: The word shifted once more, and this time it left the page entirely.
quit:0.line: 'Do not *quit* — a word only opens when it feels you will wait.'

recall:0.en: Master Qingwu asked me to close my eyes and *recall* the first word I had ever read aloud in the hall. The memory rose slowly, pale and uncertain. Then it sharpened, and with it came a warmth at my fingertips I had not felt since that first morning. Somewhere above us, a bell rang that no one had struck.
recall:0.cnHint: 师尊让我闭眼____我在大殿中大声念出的第一个词，那份记忆带来了奇异的温暖。
recall:0.hook: The bell rang a second time, and its echo moved downward, not up.
recall:0.line: '*Recall* the first word you loved, and it will still remember you.'

register:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long scroll of pale cloud-silk and pressed my finger to the bottom line. 'Every disciple who enters the sect must *register* their true name here,' she said. The ink glowed soft gold where I touched it, then faded to silver. My name was now part of the mountain.
register:0.cnHint: 新弟子在入门卷轴上____自己的名字，墨迹发出金光。
register:0.hook: But the silver ink began, slowly, to turn black.
register:0.line: 'You must *register* your name before the candle burns out.'

skin:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a small jade bowl. Inside lay a pale leaf, thin as paper. 'Press it to your *skin*,' he said quietly. I placed it on my wrist. Cool light spread through my arm, and for one breath I could feel every root of every herb growing on the mountain below.
skin:0.cnHint: 师兄让我把叶片贴在____上，奇异的凉意随即蔓延全身。
skin:0.hook: Then the leaf turned ash-grey and crumbled without a sound.
skin:0.line: 'The herb reads your *skin* before it chooses to heal you.'
