spirit:0.en: The inner hall was still. Master Qingwu placed a single candle between us and told me to say the word for 'wind' until I felt something move that was not air. On my fourth try a warmth rose behind my ribs. 'That,' she said, 'is your *spirit* waking.' Outside, the clouds began to spin.
spirit:0.cnHint: 师尊教我念风字诀，直到内心深处的____苏醒过来。
spirit:0.hook: The candle flame bent sideways, though all windows were shut.
spirit:0.line: 'A strong *spirit* is the root from which all words grow.'

spread:0.en: Xiaoxing laid five word-cards on the stone table in a neat row. As she whispered each one, pale light began to *spread* from card to card like water crossing silk, linking them into a single shining line. 'A formula is never one word alone,' she told me with a small smile. The light pulsed once, then held.
spread:0.cnHint: 师妹低声念出字诀，光芒从一张卡____向下一张，连成一线。
spread:0.hook: The sixth card, blank and untouched, lit up on its own.
spread:0.line: 'Watch how the light will *spread* when the words trust each other.'

totally:0.en: I tried the lifting word three times and rose no higher than a finger's width before dropping back to the floor. Shen Wujiu did not laugh. 'You are not *totally* wrong in your breath,' he said, 'but you are gripping the sound instead of releasing it.' On my fourth try I lifted a full foot, and the floor felt very far away.
totally:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，我的呼吸法并非____错误，只是还不够放松。
totally:0.hook: A sharp crack echoed from the stone floor beneath my feet.
totally:0.line: 'You are not *totally* wrong — only the last breath needs to open.'

tree:0.en: Near the east window stood a small clay pot holding a *tree* no taller than my hand. Its trunk was wound with a paper strip covered in tiny characters. Master Qingwu said each character was a word the tree had absorbed over a hundred years of lessons. I leaned close; I was almost certain I heard it breathe.
tree:0.cnHint: 东窗边有一棵____，树干上缠绕着写满字诀的纸条。
tree:0.hook: One character on the strip was still moving, rearranging itself slowly.
tree:0.line: 'This *tree* has listened to more words than you have spoken in your life.'

weigh:0.en: Before she would teach me a new formula, Master Qingwu made me hold its word-card in both hands and simply wait. 'You must *weigh* it,' she said, 'feel whether it sits heavy or light in you.' The card for 'stone' pressed down like a river rock. The card for 'feather' nearly lifted my hands from below.
weigh:0.cnHint: 师尊要我用双手____每个字诀的分量，感受它的轻重。
weigh:0.hook: The card for 'sky' burned cold and did not register any weight at all.
weigh:0.line: '*Weigh* the word first — a formula cast too soon will break its own shape.'

alive:0.en: Shen Wujiu set an ink stone before me and said nothing for a long moment. Then: 'Write the word for fire.' I brushed it slowly. The character dried — and glowed. 'When a word is written with full breath and clear mind,' he said softly, 'it stays *alive* on the page.' A thin curl of warm smoke rose from the paper.
alive:0.cnHint: 师兄说，用完整的气息书写字诀，它就会在纸上保持____。
alive:0.hook: The smoke formed a shape — then dissolved before I could name it.
alive:0.line: 'Every word you write with true breath comes out *alive*.'

anyway:0.en: The hall smelled of pine resin and old ink. Master Qingwu set a single scroll before me and said nothing. I had not slept; my hands were cold; the characters swam before my eyes. None of that mattered. I pressed my brush to the page *anyway*, and the first stroke glowed a pale, steady gold.
anyway:0.cnHint: 尽管疲惫不堪，我____提起笔，第一笔竟发出金光。
anyway:0.hook: The glow faded — and left a shadow shaped like a warning.
anyway:0.line: 'You are tired and afraid, but write *anyway* — the word will decide the rest.'

arise:0.en: I knelt on the cold stone floor of the inner hall, watching Master Qingwu trace a formula in the air. She explained that storms over the Cloud Sea do not come from the sky above — they *arise* from the words disciples speak carelessly at night, drifting downward like seed and taking root in the wind.
arise:0.cnHint: 师尊解释道，云海上的风暴会从弟子随意说出的话语中____。
arise:0.hook: Outside, a single candle flame bent toward me without any wind.
arise:0.line: 'Know this: great trials *arise* not from the heavens but from careless tongues.'

besides:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread three jars on the study table. Two held common ink; the third held something silver that moved on its own. He told me the silver formula could copy any text I had already memorized. *Besides*, he added quietly, it could hold a copied text safe even if my memory later failed.
besides:0.cnHint: 师兄介绍了银色墨水的用途，____还说它能保存我记忆中的文字。
besides:0.hook: The silver ink stilled, then spelled one unasked character on its own.
besides:0.line: 'It copies what you know. *Besides*, it remembers what you forget.'

certainly:0.en: Xiaoxing held the lamp steady while I read aloud the healing formula for the third time. My voice was uncertain, but the herb-characters on the page began to rise in thin green smoke. She turned to me with calm eyes. '*Certainly* you feel it now,' she said — and I did: a warm current moving up my wrist.
certainly:0.cnHint: 小星平静地说，我____感受到了疗愈咒文的力量，温热从手腕升起。
certainly:0.hook: The green smoke formed a character no page in the hall had ever shown.
certainly:0.line: '*Certainly* you feel the warmth — the formula has chosen to answer you.'

challenging:0.en: The morning lesson was *challenging* in a way silence can be: Master Qingwu placed an empty page before me and left the room. No prompt, no model script, no sound but the distant sea of clouds shifting far below. I stared at the blank surface until a single character rose in my mind, clear and uninvited.
challenging:0.cnHint: 早课令人____——师尊留下一张空白纸页就离开了，我独自面对沉默。
challenging:0.hook: The uninvited character was not one I had ever been taught.
challenging:0.line: 'A blank page is *challenging*, but what rises from silence is yours alone.'

circumstance:0.en: Shen Wujiu found me copying the same line for the sixth time, ink smeared, breath tight. He sat beside me without judgement and said that a word planted under difficult *circumstance* takes deeper root than one written in ease. He tapped the smeared line gently; under his finger, the ink cleared and held.
circumstance:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，在艰难____下写下的文字，往往比安逸时扎根更深。
circumstance:0.hook: The cleared ink shimmered once — then began to rewrite itself.
circumstance:0.line: 'In every hard *circumstance*, the word you press through becomes your strongest root.'

comfort:0.en: The study fire had burned low. Xiaoxing brought me a bowl of warm water and set it without a word by my elbow. It was a small thing, but in that silent hall the *comfort* of it reached further than any spoken encouragement. I steadied my brush, and the next character came out clean and true.
comfort:0.cnHint: 小星送来一碗温水，那份____让我在寂静的书房里重新稳住了心神。
comfort:0.hook: At the bowl's still surface, a tiny character appeared, then vanished.
comfort:0.line: 'Take this small *comfort* — a steady hand begins with a steady heart.'

enrich:0.en: Master Qingwu told us that copying a formula once plants a seed; reading it aloud waters the seed; but only living by its meaning will *enrich* the ground enough for the word to grow into something that flies. She closed the lesson there, leaving the last line of the scroll still rolled and hidden from view.
enrich:0.cnHint: 师尊说，只有真正践行咒文的含义，才能____土壤，让文字真正生长飞升。
enrich:0.hook: The hidden last line of the scroll moved, as though something inside it breathed.
enrich:0.line: 'Practice alone cannot *enrich* the word — you must live what it asks of you.'

facilitate:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long scroll across the stone table. 'These ancient formulas,' she said quietly, 'will *facilitate* your first attempt at inner-breath control.' She placed each word-herb in order, one beside the next, until the sequence glowed faint gold. I copied every mark with care, feeling the air in the hall grow warmer with each stroke.
facilitate:0.cnHint: 师尊将古老的符文排列好，以____我们学习内息控制。
facilitate:0.hook: But the last word on the scroll had already begun to fade.
facilitate:0.line: 'These formulas will *facilitate* your climb, if you trust them.'

insight:0.en: Shen Wujiu sat across from me in the inner study, turning a single word-herb between his fingers. 'Stare at it long enough,' he said, 'and you will gain *insight* into what it truly asks of you.' I stared. The character blurred, then sharpened, and for one breath I understood the cloud beneath our mountain as if I had always lived inside it.
insight:0.cnHint: 师兄说，凝视那枚字草足够久，你便能对它有所____。
insight:0.hook: Then the word-herb cracked clean down the middle.
insight:0.line: 'Real *insight* comes only when you stop trying to force it.'

preparation:0.en: The night before the ascent trial, I spread every word-herb I owned across my sleeping mat. *Preparation*, Xiaoxing had told me earlier that evening, was itself a kind of silent prayer. I arranged the herbs by tone and weight, the way she showed me, and the room filled with a low hum, as though the mountain approved.
preparation:0.cnHint: 小星说，____本身就是一种无声的祈祷。
preparation:0.hook: Somewhere below the clouds, a bell rang once and did not stop.
preparation:0.line: 'Your *preparation* tonight will decide what the mountain shows you.'

separate:0.en: Master Qingwu asked me to *separate* the gold-vein herbs from the grey ones before dawn. I worked by candlelight, sorting each word into its own small bowl. The task seemed simple until I found one herb that glowed both colours at once, refusing to belong to either side, pulsing softly like a question I did not yet know how to ask.
separate:0.cnHint: 师尊让我在黎明前把金脉字草与灰色字草____开来。
separate:0.hook: The two-coloured herb was gone by the time the candle burned out.
separate:0.line: '*Separate* them carefully — some words carry more than one truth.'

tie:0.en: Xiaoxing showed me how to *tie* the word-scrolls into a bundle before storing them in the archive shelf. 'The knot matters,' she said with a small smile. 'A loose tie lets the meaning drift.' I pulled the cord tight and felt a faint warmth travel up my fingers, as if the scrolls were grateful to be held together at last.
tie:0.cnHint: 小星教我如何把字卷____成一束，说结扣本身也有意义。
tie:0.hook: One scroll at the bottom of the bundle was already warm before I touched it.
tie:0.line: '*Tie* them firmly — a wandering word can wake the wrong wind.'

jam:0.en: The archive door would not open. Shen Wujiu pushed his shoulder against it twice and shook his head. 'The old humidity makes it *jam*,' he said, then pressed a breath-word to the frame, and the door released with a sigh of cedar-scented air. Inside, every shelf was in order — except one, where a single scroll lay open on the floor.
jam:0.cnHint: 师兄说旧湿气会让门____住，然后用一个气字将它打开。
jam:0.hook: The open scroll on the floor showed words none of us had written.
jam:0.line: 'Damp air can *jam* more than a door — check the seals tonight.'

supermarket:0.en: During the New-Disciple Fair, the sect's trading hall was so full of word-herbs and formula cards that Xiaoxing laughed and called it a *supermarket* of the spirit path. I did not know the word, but the meaning was clear enough: every shelf overflowed, every stall competed for your gaze. I bought a single small herb and felt richer than I deserved.
supermarket:0.cnHint: 小星笑着把门派的交易大厅比作修行路上的____。
supermarket:0.hook: One stall in the far corner had no sign and sold nothing — only watched.
supermarket:0.line: 'This hall is our *supermarket* — but the rarest words are never on display.'

debate:0.en: A quiet *debate* filled the inner study all afternoon. Shen Wujiu believed the fire-breath formula should come before the wind one; Master Qingwu held the opposite view and said nothing more than was needed. I listened from the doorway, not daring to enter, learning more from their silence than from the words they actually exchanged.
debate:0.cnHint: 整个下午，师兄和师尊在内室就修炼顺序展开了一场____。
debate:0.hook: When they finally agreed, every candle in the room bent toward the window.
debate:0.line: 'We can *debate* the order, but the mountain will choose for you in the end.'

egg:0.en: Inside the inner hall, Master Qingwu placed a smooth stone on the altar. 'This is no ordinary stone,' she said. 'It is an *egg* — a seed-word carrying an entire formula within its shell. Crack it open with your mind and the sky-walking technique will hatch.' I pressed my palm against it and felt something stir.
egg:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊告诉我，祭坛上的石头其实是一枚____，内藏飞升法诀。
egg:0.hook: A faint crack split the stone — and the hall lights died.
egg:0.line: 'This *egg* holds a sky-walking formula — crack it with your will.'

hire:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread a scroll across the study table and tapped a red seal at its bottom. 'The Sect did not simply accept you,' he said quietly. 'They *hire* every new disciple to tend the Word Garden for one full year before any advanced study begins.' I stared at the seal. It glowed like a small coal.
hire:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，宗门____新弟子的条件是先照料文字灵园整整一年。
hire:0.hook: The seal pulsed once — as if it had just heard my name.
hire:0.line: 'They *hire* each disciple to guard the Word Garden before all else.'

aid:0.en: In the archive room, Xiaoxing handed me a thin jade slip. 'Keep this close,' she whispered. 'It holds the first-aid word — a formula that can *aid* any disciple who loses control of a rising technique.' The slip felt cool against my palm, like still water before a storm breaks.
aid:0.cnHint: 小星师妹给了我一枚玉简，说其中的____字诀能在法术失控时救人。
aid:0.hook: The jade slip grew warm without warning, as if someone nearby had already lost control.
aid:0.line: 'This word can *aid* you the moment a technique turns against you.'

bill:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long paper on the reading desk. It listed every word-herb I had consumed since entering the Sect. 'Consider this your first *bill*,' she said without warmth. 'Words have cost. You will repay each one through practice.' The total at the bottom glowed faintly gold.
bill:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊展示了我入门以来耗用灵词的____，并告知须以修炼偿还。
bill:0.hook: At the very foot of the bill, one item had no price — only a question mark.
bill:0.line: 'This *bill* records every word-herb you have consumed since your first day.'

paint:0.en: Xiaoxing dipped a brush in silver ink and began to *paint* the ascent formula across the inner wall of our study room. Each stroke released a soft hum, as if the word wanted to lift free of the plaster. 'Do not step inside the lines,' she warned, 'until Master Qingwu says the pattern is complete.'
paint:0.cnHint: 小星师妹用银墨在书室内壁____飞升法阵，并警告我不要踏入阵线。
paint:0.hook: One brushstroke moved on its own while Xiaoxing set the brush down.
paint:0.line: 'I will *paint* the full ascent pattern before the evening bell sounds.'

bean:0.en: On the shelf above my sleeping mat sat a single dried *bean* — small, dark, and marked with one silver character. Shen Wujiu had left it there without explanation. When I finally read the character aloud, the whole room filled with the scent of high-altitude wind, cold and clean and impossibly far up.
bean:0.cnHint: 师兄在我床头留下一粒刻有灵字的____，我朗读字符后房间充满了高空的气息。
bean:0.hook: The bean crumbled to dust — and the silver character hung in the air.
bean:0.line: 'One *bean* from the Word Garden can open a path you never expected.'

birthday:0.en: Shen Wujiu set a small lamp on the study table and lit it without ceremony. 'Today is the Sect's founding day,' he said. 'We call it the *birthday* of the first word-formula — the one that lifted this mountain from the sea of clouds.' The flame burned blue, not gold, and did not flicker once.
birthday:0.cnHint: 师兄点燃灯火，说今天是第一道灵诀诞生的____，也是宗门的建立之日。
birthday:0.hook: The blue flame split into two — and neither half cast a shadow.
birthday:0.line: 'This flame marks the *birthday* of the first formula our Sect ever spoke.'

flight:0.en: Inside the preparation hall, Master Qingwu drew a single character on the floor with her finger. The stroke glowed and then rose, hovering at eye level. 'That word means *flight*,' she said. 'It is not a gift. It is a question the sky asks you. Answer it correctly and you rise. Answer it wrong and you fall.'
flight:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊在备课堂地面写下一个代表____的灵字，并说那是天空对弟子的考验。
flight:0.hook: The glowing character slowly turned to face me — and waited.
flight:0.line: 'This word means *flight* — and the sky will ask it of you before long.'

partly:0.en: The inner hall was *partly* lit by a single spirit-lantern, its pale glow falling only on the nearest shelves of herb-jars. The rest of the room held shadows that breathed. Master Qingwu stood at the far edge of the light, watching me arrange the morning offerings without a word.
partly:0.cnHint: 内殿只有____被灵灯照亮，师尊在光影边缘默默注视着我。
partly:0.hook: Something in the dark corner had just moved.
partly:0.line: 'The room is *partly* prepared — but the most important shelf remains untouched.'

practical:0.en: Shen Wujiu laid three herb-bundles on the low table and told me that beautiful theory fills no cauldron. Every formula I had memorized this month, he said, must now be tested in a *practical* way — by mixing, heating, and tasting the result myself, with no second chance if the smoke turned grey.
practical:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，所有的心法都必须用____的方式来检验。
practical:0.hook: The smoke above the cauldron was already turning grey.
practical:0.line: 'A *practical* test will show what your memory cannot.'

profit:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a yellowed record of the sect's herb trades. She said a disciple who studies words only for personal *profit* poisons every formula they touch. True mastery, she told me, flows toward others like mountain water — downward, freely, without asking a price.
profit:0.cnHint: 师尊展开账册，告诫我不能只为个人____而修炼字道。
profit:0.hook: One name in the record had been crossed out in red.
profit:0.line: 'There is no lasting *profit* in hoarding what words were meant to share.'

promise:0.en: Xiaoxing pressed a small jade slip into my hand before dawn and whispered that it held the formula I had been seeking. She asked only one thing in return: a *promise* that I would stand beside her when the Trial of Ascending Wind came, whatever the cost.
promise:0.cnHint: 小星在拂晓前递给我一块玉简，只求我给她一个____。
promise:0.hook: The jade slip was warmer than it should have been.
promise:0.line: 'Give me your *promise*, and the formula is yours before sunrise.'

rarely:0.en: The archive room smelled of age and cedar. Master Qingwu told me that she *rarely* opened this cabinet — perhaps once in ten years — because the scrolls inside responded to doubt, and even she still carried doubt about the highest formulas. She set a single candle on the shelf and stepped back.
rarely:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，这个柜子她____打开，因为里面的卷轴能感知疑惑。
rarely:0.hook: The candle flame leaned toward the closed cabinet door.
rarely:0.line: 'I *rarely* stand here — the scrolls remember every uncertain heart.'

severe:0.en: The punishment room at the back of the hall was plain and cold. Shen Wujiu said the *severe* silence in that room was itself the lesson — no herb, no light, only the sound of your own breathing until you understood what you had broken. He had spent three nights there once. He did not smile when he said it.
severe:0.cnHint: 师兄说那间静室____的寂静本身就是惩罚。
severe:0.hook: From behind the closed door came one slow, measured breath.
severe:0.line: 'The silence inside is *severe* enough to crack an unprepared mind.'

smell:0.en: I entered the preparation room and stopped. The *smell* that reached me was wrong — not cedar and dried root as usual, but something sharp and faintly sweet, like a formula that had been left to decay. Xiaoxing was already there, kneeling beside an overturned jar, her face pale.
smell:0.cnHint: 我走进备药室，闻到一股异常的____，小星跪在翻倒的药罐旁，脸色苍白。
smell:0.hook: The sweet decay in the air was slowly growing stronger.
smell:0.line: 'That *smell* means something inside this jar has already changed.'

socialize:0.en: After the evening lesson, Shen Wujiu urged me to *socialize* with the other disciples in the common hall rather than returning alone to my room. He said those quiet conversations over warm tea were themselves a kind of cultivation — that words learned among friends carried more life than words studied in silence.
socialize:0.cnHint: 晚课后，师兄劝我去公共厅与同门____，而不是独自回房。
socialize:0.hook: Through the common-hall window, one disciple sat perfectly still.
socialize:0.line: 'If you never *socialize*, you will master words but forget their warmth.'

housing:0.en: Master Qingwu led us through the inner hall, where each new disciple was assigned a chamber carved from living stone. 'The sect provides *housing* for every disciple who earns their place,' she said, pressing a jade token into my palm. The room smelled of cedar and old ink. That night, a crack appeared across my ceiling, shaped like a flying crane.
housing:0.cnHint: 师尊将我们带到内殿，说宗门会为每位弟子提供____，并给了我一块玉牌。
housing:0.hook: The crack on the ceiling grew one inch wider before dawn.
housing:0.line: 'The sect provides *housing* for every disciple who earns their place.'

behaviour:0.en: Shen Wujiu watched me copy the healing word three times and shook his head slowly. 'Master Qingwu judges a disciple not by talent alone, but by *behaviour* inside the hall,' he said. 'Every bow, every silence, every small choice is seen.' I set my brush down more carefully after that. A pale moth landed on the ink stone and did not move.
behaviour:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，师尊不只看才能，更看弟子在殿内的____。
behaviour:0.hook: The moth's wings bore the exact shape of the word I had just written.
behaviour:0.line: 'Master Qingwu judges a disciple not by talent alone, but by *behaviour* inside the hall.'

husband:0.en: Xiaoxing showed me a faded portrait hanging near the archive shelf. The man in it had kind eyes and worn robes. 'He was Master Qingwu's *husband*,' she whispered, 'a word-keeper who sealed the great rift above the eastern peak thirty years ago.' The portrait held no name, only a single character burned into the silk. A cold draft moved through the sealed room.
husband:0.cnHint: 小星指着画像悄声说，画中人是师尊的____，曾以文字之力封印了东峰上方的裂缝。
husband:0.hook: The burned character on the silk began, very slowly, to glow.
husband:0.line: 'He was Master Qingwu's *husband*, a word-keeper who sealed the great rift.'

tourist:0.en: A stranger wandered into the outer library with wide eyes and muddy boots, touching every scroll case without permission. Shen Wujiu stepped forward calmly. 'This hall is not open to any *tourist* who drifts in from the cloud-road,' he said, voice low but firm. The stranger left without a word. Behind the door, the oldest scroll case began to hum.
tourist:0.cnHint: 一个外来者闯入藏经阁，师兄平静地告诉他，这里不对____开放。
tourist:0.hook: The humming grew louder the moment the stranger's footsteps faded.
tourist:0.line: 'This hall is not open to any *tourist* who drifts in from the cloud-road.'

agent:0.en: A sealed letter arrived during morning study, marked with three black rings. Xiaoxing read it first and went pale. 'Someone sent an *agent* into the lower archive last night,' she said, sliding the letter across the desk to me. 'They were looking for the suppression word.' The candle between us guttered once, though the air was perfectly still.
agent:0.cnHint: 小星读完密信后脸色发白，说有人派了____昨夜潜入下层书库寻找镇压咒文。
agent:0.hook: The candle flame turned a brief, vivid green before steadying.
agent:0.line: 'Someone sent an *agent* into the lower archive last night.'

cash:0.en: The sect's supply elder spread her ledger on the study table and sighed. 'Rare ink herbs cannot be traded in kind this season. We need *cash* from the cloud market below, or the archive lamps will run dry by winter.' Master Qingwu listened without expression and then wrote a single word on a strip of paper. The strip folded itself into a crane and flew out the window.
cash:0.cnHint: 供应长老说，这一季珍贵的墨草无法以物易物，必须有____才能从云市购得。
cash:0.hook: No one saw where the paper crane landed in the sea of clouds below.
cash:0.line: 'We need *cash* from the cloud market below, or the archive lamps will run dry.'

competition:0.en: The inner hall held its annual word-recitation trial at dawn. Shen Wujiu leaned close before I stepped forward. 'Do not let the *competition* make you rush,' he murmured. 'A word spoken in panic loses half its power.' I breathed, walked to the center stone, and spoke the healing word cleanly. Every lamp in the hall flared gold at once.
competition:0.cnHint: 在宗门年度背诵考核中，师兄提醒我不要因为____而慌乱失措。
competition:0.hook: The gold faded — all except one lamp, directly above my head.
competition:0.line: 'Do not let the *competition* make you rush — a panicked word loses its power.'

farmer:0.en: An old man arrived at the sect gate at midday, carrying a bundle of dried cloud-root on his back. 'I am only a *farmer* from the lower mist fields,' he told the gate disciple, 'but I grew these roots from seeds your Master gave my grandfather.' Xiaoxing brought the bundle inside without hesitation. That evening, Master Qingwu pressed one root to her lips and closed her eyes for a long moment.
farmer:0.cnHint: 一位来自下层雾田的____带着亲手种植的云根草来到宗门山门前。
farmer:0.hook: When Master Qingwu opened her eyes, they were a shade brighter than before.
farmer:0.line: 'I am only a *farmer* from the lower mist fields, but these roots carry your Master's gift.'

collection:0.en: Master Qingwu led me into the inner hall, where scroll after scroll lined the stone walls from floor to ceiling. 'This *collection* holds every word-formula our sect has recovered in three hundred years,' she said softly. Each scroll glowed faintly, as if breathing. I reached toward the nearest one — and it pulled back on its own.
collection:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊带我进入内殿，展示门派三百年来积累的所有字诀____。
collection:0.hook: One scroll at the far end burned cold blue, and no name was written on it.
collection:0.line: 'This *collection* holds every word-formula our sect has recovered in three hundred years.'

depression:0.en: I sat alone at the edge of the study room after failing the morning recitation for the third day. A heavy *depression* settled in my chest like wet clay. Xiaoxing set a warm cup beside me without a word. Outside, the clouds beneath the mountain shifted — and for a moment they spelled a shape I almost recognised.
depression:0.cnHint: 连续三天背诵失败后，我独自坐在书房角落，心中充满____。
depression:0.hook: The cloud-shape dissolved before I could read it, leaving only the smell of coming rain.
depression:0.line: 'A little *depression* after three failures is honest — but the fourth attempt is what counts.'

foot:0.en: The inner sanctum door stood exactly one *foot* above the floor, raised on a carved stone step worn smooth by ten thousand crossings. Shen Wujiu told me the gap was deliberate: a disciple who did not lower their head to enter had no business inside. I lowered mine — and heard the door seal shut behind me.
foot:0.cnHint: 内殿门槛高出地面整整一____，要求弟子低头而入。
foot:0.hook: Through the sealed stone, a second heartbeat tapped back at mine.
foot:0.line: 'The step is exactly one *foot* high — the sect built humility into the architecture.'

graduate:0.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled a list of names on the long study table. 'Every *graduate* of the Cloud Sea Sect signed here before their final ascent,' he said. The oldest signatures had faded to silver dust. Mine was supposed to appear at the bottom — but when I looked, the last line was already filled with a name I did not know.
graduate:0.cnHint: 师兄展示历代____在飞升前亲笔签下的名单，我却发现末尾已有陌生名字。
graduate:0.hook: The unknown name was written in ink that was still wet.
graduate:0.line: 'Every *graduate* of our sect signed this list — read the oldest names if you want courage.'

intake:0.en: Master Qingwu watched my breathing during the word-absorption trial. 'Slow your *intake*,' she said, 'or the formula will burn the channel before it settles.' I steadied my breath, and the character for 'sky' dissolved into warm light along my ribs. Then the room temperature dropped sharply, and every candle flame bent toward the window.
intake:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊在字诀吸收试炼中叮嘱我放缓____，以免灼伤经脉。
intake:0.hook: Every flame pointed at the same dark corner, where nothing visible stood.
intake:0.line: 'Slow your *intake* — let the word settle before you draw the next breath.'

screen:0.en: A tall paper *screen* divided the preparation hall, painted with clouds and cranes in fading ink. Master Qingwu sat behind it during our oral trials so that a student's face would not influence her judgment. I recited the three ascent formulas without error. As I finished, a crack split the screen from top to bottom — though no one had touched it.
screen:0.cnHint: 内堂以绘有云鹤的纸质____隔开，师尊在其后主持口试以示公正。
screen:0.hook: Through the crack, I saw not the wall behind the screen, but open sky.
screen:0.line: 'The *screen* keeps my eyes honest — I judge the word, not the speaker.'

chair:0.en: At the centre of the archive room stood a single stone *chair*, reserved, Shen Wujiu said, for whoever could recite all one hundred root-words without pause. No disciple had sat in it for sixty years. On a dare to myself I began to recite — and reached the ninety-seventh word before my voice caught. The chair slid one inch toward me.
chair:0.cnHint: 档案室中央有一把石____，专为能不停顿背完百个根字的弟子而设，已空置六十年。
chair:0.hook: The chair did not slide back, and the room had no draft.
chair:0.line: 'No one has earned that *chair* in sixty years — but the sect keeps it polished just in case.'

court:0.en: The covered walkway opened onto a small inner *court* paved with white stone, used for the formal presentation of new disciples to the elder records. Master Qingwu read my name aloud, and the stones hummed once in reply. Xiaoxing squeezed my hand for just a moment. Above us, a single dark cloud crossed the sun and did not move on.
court:0.cnHint: 有顶回廊通向铺着白石的内____，用于新弟子正式入册的仪式。
court:0.hook: The cloud held its position as if it, too, were waiting to hear what came next.
court:0.line: 'Stand still in the *court* — the stones only hum for names the mountain accepts.'

female:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old pine and dried cloud-moss. Master Qingwu placed two spirit jars on the stone table — one carved with a sun mark, one with a moon. 'The moon jar,' she said, 'belongs to the *female* crane that guards the east peak. Return it before dawn, or she will not let you pass.' I picked it up with both hands, feeling its cold weight.
female:0.cnHint: 师尊说，月形罐子属于守护东峰的____丹顶鹤，必须在黎明前归还。
female:0.hook: Outside, something large shifted its wings in the dark.
female:0.line: 'This moon jar belongs to the *female* crane — do not lose it.'

holiday:0.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled a paper scroll across the low table. 'Tomorrow is the Cloud Sea *holiday*,' he said quietly, 'the one day each year when the sect opens its sealed word-garden to new disciples.' He traced a path with his finger. 'Master Qingwu says only three may enter. There are four of us.' The candle between us did not flicker, yet somehow it seemed smaller.
holiday:0.cnHint: 师兄说，明天是云海____，封印词园唯一对新弟子开放的日子，但名额只有三个。
holiday:0.hook: Somewhere in the hall, a door clicked shut that no one had opened.
holiday:0.line: 'On this *holiday*, the word-garden chooses — not us.'

pain:0.en: I pressed my palm flat against the practice stone and spoke the word for wind. Nothing moved. I tried again. A sharp heat spread up my wrist — not the clean warmth of a flowing formula, but the raw *pain* of a word spoken wrong. Xiaoxing looked up from her own stone. 'That sound,' she said softly, 'means the character is resisting you.' In the corner, Master Qingwu said nothing, only watched.
pain:0.cnHint: 我错误地念出了风字，手腕传来____，师妹说这意味着那个字在抵抗我。
pain:0.hook: The practice stone held a crack now that had not been there before.
pain:0.line: 'That *pain* in your wrist means the word heard something wrong.'

player:0.en: The sect kept a word-game called the Mirror Round, played on a board of carved cloud-jade. Shen Wujiu set the pieces out slowly. 'Each *player* picks a word-stone and places it where its meaning connects to another,' he explained. 'The board decides if the link is true.' I reached for the stone marked 'ascend.' The board gave a low tone — neither approval nor refusal — and the room felt suddenly still.
player:0.cnHint: 师兄解释说，在镜局游戏里，每位____选一块词石，摆在与其含义相连的位置，棋盘会判断是否成立。
player:0.hook: My stone had moved one space on its own by the time I looked back.
player:0.line: 'Every *player* must choose a word they truly understand — the board will know.'

production:0.en: The inner archive held rows of small clay tablets, each stamped with a formula. Master Qingwu lifted one and held it to the lamp. 'This is the earliest *production* of the Cloud Sea Sect,' she said, 'made in the founding year, when the first master pressed living words into clay before they could fade.' The tablet glowed faintly orange, as though something inside still breathed. She set it down and did not let us touch it.
production:0.cnHint: 师尊展示了云海宗最早的____，建宗之年第一位掌门将活字压入泥板，以防消散。
production:0.hook: One tablet at the far end of the shelf was warm to the eye, not the hand.
production:0.line: 'This *production* of the first master still holds a living word inside.'

secure:0.en: Xiaoxing knelt by the archive door and looped a cord of woven cloud-silk three times through the iron ring. 'You have to make it *secure* at both ends,' she said, 'or the door reads the formula as incomplete and will not hold overnight.' I helped her pull the final knot tight. The silk hummed once, then went quiet. Through the narrow window, the sea of clouds below had turned the pale grey of almost-morning.
secure:0.cnHint: 师妹说门必须用云丝绳在两端绑____，否则门上的法阵会视其为不完整而无法封印过夜。
secure:0.hook: The knot held — but the cord had tied itself one loop tighter than we left it.
secure:0.line: 'Pull both ends — you must make it *secure* before the formula sets.'

audience:0.en: Master Qingwu rarely granted a private meeting. When the summons came, Shen Wujiu told me to bow at the threshold and wait. 'An *audience* with her means she has seen something in your practice,' he said, folding his hands, 'something worth her direct attention.' I stood at the carved wooden door for a long breath. Inside, I could hear the soft sound of pages turning, unhurried, as if she already knew I was there.
audience:0.cnHint: 师兄说，得到师尊的____意味着她在你的修炼中察觉了值得亲自关注的事。
audience:0.hook: The pages inside stopped turning the moment my hand touched the door.
audience:0.line: 'An *audience* with Master Qingwu is not given — it is earned by what the words reveal.'

borrow:0.en: My own word-brush had a crack along the handle. Xiaoxing set hers on the table beside mine without comment. 'You can *borrow* it for tonight's copy work,' she said, 'but return it before the third bell — I need it for the dawn lesson.' The brush was lighter than it looked, and when I dipped it in the formula ink, the first character I drew came out steadier than any I had made with my own. I did not tell her that.
borrow:0.cnHint: 师妹让我____她的词笔用于今晚的抄写，但必须在三更前归还，因为她黎明课要用。
borrow:0.hook: The character I wrote had already begun to glow before the ink was dry.
borrow:0.line: 'You can *borrow* my brush — but the words you write with it are still yours.'

burn:0.en: The Pill Chamber smelled of old smoke and herbs. Master Qingwu lifted my sleeve and studied the red mark on my wrist. 'A *burn*,' she said quietly, 'left by a word-flame you were not ready to hold.' I had tried to speak the fire formula alone at midnight. The scar was proof of my pride. Outside, a cold wind pressed against the wooden door.
burn:0.cnHint: 我私自尝试念诵火焰咒语，手腕上留下了____的痕迹，师尊沉默地审视着它。
burn:0.hook: Behind the door, the flame formula whispered itself again.
burn:0.line: 'A *burn* like this means the word chose you, not the other way around.'

cook:0.en: It was my turn to *cook* for the inner hall. Shen Wujiu watched me grind dried cloudberries into the stone bowl, saying the taste of a meal reveals the state of a disciple's mind. I tried to stay calm, but my hands moved too fast and spilled half the herbs. He said nothing. The soup, when it was done, glowed faintly blue.
cook:0.cnHint: 轮到我为内堂____饭食，师兄说，一道菜的味道能看出弟子的心境。
cook:0.hook: The blue glow deepened, and no one could explain why.
cook:0.line: 'When you *cook* with a scattered mind, the herbs remember your fear.'

corporate:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled the Sect's founding scroll. 'A *corporate* oath binds every disciple,' she said, her voice even and clear. 'You do not carry your word-power alone — you carry it on behalf of all who came before you.' I pressed my palm to the warm paper and felt something old and shared move through me. The candle flame bent toward the scroll.
corporate:0.cnHint: 师尊展开宗门誓约卷轴，说每位弟子都承担着____的责任，我按掌其上，感到一股古老的力量流过。
corporate:0.hook: The flame bent again, though the air in the room was still.
corporate:0.line: 'A *corporate* vow means your failure is never yours alone.'

dangerous:0.en: Xiaoxing spread the word-chart across the floor. 'This one,' she said, pointing to a dark glyph, 'is *dangerous* — it can lift you above the cloud layer, but if your breath falters even once, you fall.' I leaned closer. The glyph seemed to pulse like a slow heartbeat. She folded the chart before I could study it further. Snow began to fall inside the room.
dangerous:0.cnHint: 师妹展示了一个____的字符，它能让人飞越云层，但一旦呼吸中断便会坠落。
dangerous:0.hook: Snow inside a sealed room meant something was already listening.
dangerous:0.line: '*Dangerous* words are not forbidden — they are simply unforgiving.'

debt:0.en: Shen Wujiu paid for my entrance exam with three years of his own spirit-hours. I did not learn this until Master Qingwu told me quietly one evening. 'You carry a *debt*,' she said, 'not of coins, but of effort freely given.' I looked at the door through which Shen Wujiu had just walked and felt the weight of it settle across my shoulders. A single bell rang across the mountain.
debt:0.cnHint: 师兄用三年修炼时光为我垫付了入门考核的代价，师尊告诉我，这份____我须铭记于心。
debt:0.hook: The bell rang once more, though no one had touched it.
debt:0.line: 'A *debt* of spirit is harder to repay than any sum of gold.'

discipline:0.en: Master Qingwu called the morning review a matter of *discipline*, not punishment. We stood in the inner hall and recited twelve word-forms before breakfast, even on cold days when the clouds rose up past the window ledges. I stumbled on the seventh form. She did not correct me aloud — she simply waited, still as stone, until I found the right shape myself. A thin crack appeared in the far wall.
discipline:0.cnHint: 师尊说每日晨课是一种____，我在第七式上出了差错，她沉默等待，直到我自己找到正确的形态。
discipline:0.hook: The crack in the wall had not been there the day before.
discipline:0.line: '*Discipline* is the only bridge between knowing a word and owning it.'

error:0.en: I copied the healing formula onto silk paper and brought it to Shen Wujiu. He read it once, then set it down. 'There is one *error*,' he said, tapping the third line gently. 'That single wrong stroke turns a cure into a slow fever.' I felt cold. I had nearly given that formula to Xiaoxing, who had been coughing all week. The ink on the silk began to run.
error:0.cnHint: 我誊抄治愈咒语时出现了一个____，师兄指出，这一错误会把疗愈变成慢性发热。
error:0.hook: The ink kept running until the third line was gone.
error:0.line: 'One *error* in a word-formula is enough to change everything it touches.'

gym:0.en: The sect's training hall was nothing like what I had imagined. There was no soft floor or bright light — just bare stone and old ropes hanging from the ceiling. Xiaoxing called it the *gym* of the spirit: a place where the body learns to carry the weight of words. I lifted the first practice stone and felt a hum rise through my palms. The ropes began to sway without wind.
gym:0.cnHint: 宗门的修炼厅空旷而简陋，师妹称它为精神的____，我举起第一块练习石，双掌传来嗡鸣。
gym:0.hook: The ropes swayed long after every disciple had gone still.
gym:0.line: 'Every hour in this *gym* is an hour your words grow heavier and truer.'

mile:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled an old scroll across the stone table. 'Every word you learn,' she said, 'carries you one *mile* closer to the sky.' I traced the first character with my finger, and a faint warmth rose from the ink, as though the word itself remembered every disciple who had spoken it before me. Outside, the wind turned still.
mile:0.cnHint: 清雾师尊说，每掌握一个词语，就像向天空迈进一____。
mile:0.hook: Then the scroll's final line began to glow on its own.
mile:0.line: 'Each *mile* you travel begins with a single word spoken true.'

movement:0.en: Shen Wujiu stood at the center of the practice hall, eyes closed. 'Watch the *movement* of the brush,' he told me, 'not the ink.' His hand swept once across the air, and the word for wind appeared in pale light, drifting like smoke before it dissolved. I copied his gesture, and something in the room shifted.
movement:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，要观察毛笔的____，而不是墨迹本身。
movement:0.hook: My copy of the word did not dissolve — it hung there, trembling.
movement:0.line: 'The *movement* of your hand must carry the meaning, not fight it.'

party:0.en: A small *party* of senior disciples gathered in the inner hall before dawn. Master Qingwu placed a sealed jar of word-ash at the center of the table — the kind used only for ceremonies of ascent. Xiaoxing stood near the back, her face unreadable. I had not been invited, yet the door had swung open at my touch.
party:0.cnHint: 一小____高阶弟子在内堂举行仪式，我并未受邀，门却自动为我开启。
party:0.hook: Inside the jar, one word glowed that none of them had written.
party:0.line: 'Our *party* must agree before the ascent seal is broken.'

rescue:0.en: The word for shelter had slipped from my memory mid-recitation, and the practice flame began to spread across the mat. Xiaoxing crossed the room in three steps and spoke a single clear word — *rescue* — pressing her palm flat against the air. The flame folded inward and went out like a held breath. She did not look proud; she looked worried.
rescue:0.cnHint: 我背诵失误导致火焰蔓延，师妹说出____，将其平息。
rescue:0.hook: She whispered, 'That word should not have worked for you.'
rescue:0.line: 'A true *rescue* asks nothing in return — remember that.'

writing:0.en: I found a wall of old *writing* deep in the sect library — characters carved so long ago the stone had grown soft around their edges. Master Qingwu had told us that forgotten words do not die; they wait. I pressed my ear to the wall the way one listens to a shell, and a voice, thin as paper, began to count.
writing:0.cnHint: 我在藏经楼深处发现一面古老的____石壁，据说遗忘的词语会在那里等待。
writing:0.hook: It was counting down, and it stopped at one.
writing:0.line: 'The *writing* on that wall has not been read in three hundred years.'

bite:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a small clay tablet stamped with a word I did not know. 'Take a *bite*,' he said, as calmly as if offering a peach. I hesitated, then pressed the corner to my lips. The taste was cold and bright, like mountain air, and the word entered me whole — meaning, sound, and memory all at once.
bite:0.cnHint: 师兄让我____一小块刻有陌生词语的泥板，那个词便整个进入了我的记忆。
bite:0.hook: But the word tasted of grief, and it was not mine.
bite:0.line: 'One small *bite* is all it takes — the word will teach the rest.'

capture:0.en: Master Qingwu drew a circle in the air above the brazier and spoke a command. The rising smoke slowed, gathered, and held its shape — a perfect spiral, frozen mid-turn. 'To *capture* a word,' she said, 'you must want to understand it, not merely own it.' The spiral held for seven breaths, then released itself gently into nothing.
capture:0.cnHint: 清雾师尊说，想要____一个词语，必须渴望理解它，而非只是占有它。
capture:0.hook: In the ash below, a new word had written itself.
capture:0.line: 'You cannot *capture* what you are not yet willing to become.'

cope:0.en: Three new scrolls arrived before breakfast, each thicker than my arm. Xiaoxing sat across from me, already on the second. 'How do you *cope* with so much at once?' I asked. She looked up, almost smiling. 'I let the words I understand carry the ones I do not.' She turned back to her reading, and I decided to try the same.
cope:0.cnHint: 面对堆积如山的新卷轴，我问师妹如何____，她的回答让我茅塞顿开。
cope:0.hook: On my first scroll, three words lit up before I even spoke them.
cope:0.line: 'You *cope* by trusting the words you already hold inside you.'

salary:0.en: Inside the archive hall, Master Qingwu unrolled a long scroll listing every disciple's monthly allowance of spirit herbs. 'A disciple's *salary* is not coin,' she said quietly, 'but the weight of knowledge given and returned.' I copied the figures, hand trembling. The numbers felt less like payment and more like a promise.
salary:0.cnHint: 师尊在典藏阁展示弟子每月所获灵草的____清单，我抄录时手不由颤抖。
salary:0.hook: At the bottom of the scroll, my name held a question mark.
salary:0.line: 'Your *salary* of herbs will double only if your mind grows still.'

shopping:0.en: Shen Wujiu led me through the inner storehouse, pulling open drawer after drawer of dried word-herbs. 'Think of this as *shopping*,' he said with a calm smile, 'but every herb you choose will shape the spells you can cast for a year.' I reached for the bright golden leaf. He gently moved my hand aside.
shopping:0.cnHint: 师兄带我在内库挑选灵草，说这就像____，但每一株都将影响我整年的修行。
shopping:0.hook: The herb I almost chose crumbled into grey ash.
shopping:0.line: '*Shopping* here is easy — choosing wisely is the hard part.'

tendency:0.en: Master Qingwu watched me write practice formulas on the stone desk and folded her hands. 'You have a *tendency* to rush the final stroke,' she said, voice soft as mist. 'Speed without stillness breaks the seal.' I looked at my work and saw it clearly: every third line ended in a small, reckless curve.
tendency:0.cnHint: 师尊观察我书写法诀时，指出我有一种____让最后一笔过于匆忙。
tendency:0.hook: The cracked seal on the desk began, slowly, to glow.
tendency:0.line: 'That *tendency* to hurry will cost you when the storm arrives.'

tough:0.en: The lowest storage cellar smelled of cold earth and old bark. Shen Wujiu handed me a root sealed in wax. 'Word-iron root,' he said. '*Tough* enough to cut glass, yet one correct syllable softens it completely.' I held it up to the dim lantern light. Something inside the root pulsed, once, like a slow heartbeat.
tough:0.cnHint: 师兄在储藏室将一株____的言铁根交给我，说唯有正确的音节才能使其柔化。
tough:0.hook: The pulse came again, quicker this time.
tough:0.line: 'It looks *tough*, but the right word will make it weep.'

tour:0.en: Xiaoxing arrived at dawn to give me a quiet *tour* of the inner hall. She named each shelf, each sealed jar, each hook where elder disciples once hung their practice scrolls. Her voice was steady and warm. By the last corridor I noticed she had skipped one narrow door entirely, eyes fixed ahead.
tour:0.cnHint: 小星在黎明带我____内堂，逐一介绍每个书架与密封罐，却悄悄跳过了一扇窄门。
tour:0.hook: The narrow door hummed a single low note as we passed.
tour:0.line: 'Every *tour* ends here — no one asks about that door.'

wake:0.en: I studied late into the night, candles burning low. When I finally lifted my head, the hall was silent. In the *wake* of so many hours of reading, the words seemed to float off the page and drift like luminous petals through the dark air. I blinked. The petals settled. One remained, hovering at eye level.
wake:0.cnHint: 深夜苦读过后，在长时间诵读的____中，我看见字符如光瓣般漂浮在空中。
wake:0.hook: The hovering petal spelled a word I had never studied.
wake:0.line: 'In the *wake* of doubt, a true disciple reads one more page.'

annual:0.en: Master Qingwu set a thick bound volume before me on the reading table. 'The sect's *annual* record,' she said, 'every disciple's growth, every failed seal, every healed wound, written down without flattery.' I opened to a random page and found a name crossed out in red. No reason was given. No other mark remained.
annual:0.cnHint: 师尊将门派的____记录摆在我面前，其中记载着每位弟子的成长与失败，我随手翻开一页，发现一个名字被红笔划去。
annual:0.hook: The crossed-out name was written in handwriting like my own.
annual:0.line: 'The *annual* record forgets no one — not even those who fled.'

charity:0.en: Xiaoxing placed a small pouch of spare word-herbs on my desk without a word. When I tried to thank her she shook her head. 'It is not *charity*,' she said, voice firm but kind. 'Strong disciples carry weak ones until the weak ones no longer need carrying. That is just the way of the sect.' She left before I could reply.
charity:0.cnHint: 小星悄悄在我桌上留下一包灵草，郑重地告诉我这并非____，而是门派的共同之道。
charity:0.hook: Outside the window, a single cloud split silently in two.
charity:0.line: 'Call it *charity* and you insult us both — call it sect-law.'

strength:0.en: Inside the Hall of Words, Master Qingwu placed three ancient scrolls on the stone table. 'A disciple does not fly on wish alone,' she said. Each scroll held a single word, and each word, when spoken with true understanding, would lend the speaker *strength* — not of muscle, but of spirit. I reached for the nearest scroll, my hand trembling only a little.
strength:0.cnHint: 师尊解释，掌握这些字卷能给弟子带来强大的____，帮助他们御风而行。
strength:0.hook: The third scroll began to glow before I even touched it.
strength:0.line: 'True *strength* lives in the word you understand, not the one you shout.'

survive:0.en: The inner library was cold even in summer. Shen Wujiu spread a worn chart across the floor and pointed to a faded red circle. 'Disciples who entered this word-zone unprepared did not *survive* the echo,' he said, voice calm, as if reading from a list of weather events. I studied the circle and told myself I would be different. The candle between us went out on its own.
survive:0.cnHint: 师兄警告说，没有充分准备进入这片区域的弟子都未能____下来。
survive:0.hook: A second candle, one I had not lit, flickered on in the corner.
survive:0.line: 'Only those who respect the word will *survive* the echo it leaves behind.'

touch:0.en: Xiaoxing handed me a small clay jar sealed with a word I could not yet read. 'Do not open it,' she said softly. 'Just feel its *touch* against your palm.' I held the jar and felt something — warmth, then a low hum, then a sudden image of open sky. Master Qingwu watched from the doorway and gave a small nod. Outside, a cloud moved against the wind.
touch:0.cnHint: 师妹让我感受那个字卷罐子的____，而不是急于将它打开。
touch:0.hook: The image of open sky had a mountain in it that did not match any I knew.
touch:0.line: 'Even a single *touch* of a living word will leave a mark on you.'

trap:0.en: The study room held a practice board where disciples could write words in spirit-ink. Shen Wujiu warned me that writing without intent was a *trap*: the word would form, but hollow, and a hollow word could turn against its speaker like a locked door springing back. I pressed the brush to the board slowly, thinking of the sky above the clouds, and the ink held its shape.
trap:0.cnHint: 师兄提醒我，无意识地书写灵字是个____，可能会伤到写字的人。
trap:0.hook: At the edge of the board, a word none of us had written began to appear on its own.
trap:0.line: 'Careless writing is a *trap* — the word hears your doubt and obeys it.'

tv:0.en: Among the sect's oldest records was a file labelled simply *tv* — an abbreviation from the world below the clouds, meaning a device that showed moving images to many people at once. Master Qingwu kept it as a curiosity, proof that the people below used light and sound to pass words around at great scale. 'We use breath,' she said. 'They used glass.' A faint hum rose from the sealed drawer.
tv:0.cnHint: 古籍中记录了云下世界用来传播图像和声音的装置，缩写为____。
tv:0.hook: The drawer had been sealed for a hundred years, yet the hum was fresh.
tv:0.line: 'They called it *tv* — a box that carried words to a thousand eyes at once.'

victim:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a teaching scroll listing errors made by past disciples. 'Every one of them,' she said quietly, 'became a *victim* of impatience — they spoke the word before they understood it, and the word answered them honestly.' The list was longer than I expected. I read each name slowly, feeling the weight of those small, honest, terrible answers. Snow fell upward past the window.
victim:0.cnHint: 师尊的教学卷轴记录了所有因急于求成而成为自身错误____的弟子。
victim:0.hook: My own name was not on the list yet, but there was space at the bottom.
victim:0.line: 'Do not be a *victim* of the very word you hoped would set you free.'

zone:0.en: Shen Wujiu walked me to the east wall of the inner hall and tapped a faint line on the floor. 'Beyond this is the silent *zone*,' he said. 'Words spoken here carry no sound, but they carry full meaning — the mountain hears them even if you do not.' I stepped across the line and felt the air change, heavier and cleaner at once, like water before rain. A low bell rang with no bell in sight.
zone:0.cnHint: 师兄带我来到内堂东墙，那里有一条分界线，线后是特殊的寂静____。
zone:0.hook: In the silent zone, I heard my own heartbeat say something back to me.
zone:0.line: 'Inside this *zone*, every word you think becomes a word the mountain knows.'

afraid:0.en: Xiaoxing found me sitting alone at the study table, the practice brush dry in my hand. 'You have not written anything in an hour,' she said. I told her I was *afraid* — not of failing, but of the word coming out right and then discovering I still did not truly understand it. She sat beside me without speaking and placed her own brush next to mine. The mountain outside shifted half a degree in the mist.
afraid:0.cnHint: 师妹发现我独坐发呆，我承认自己____，不是怕失败，而是怕成功后仍不明其意。
afraid:0.hook: When she left, both brushes had ink on them, though only one of us had moved.
afraid:0.line: 'Being *afraid* of the word means some part of you already understands its weight.'

behave:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old cedar and dried cloud-petals. Master Qingwu set a jade scroll before me and folded her hands. 'Every word you speak carries spiritual weight,' she said. 'How you *behave* in this hall shapes the energy that will follow you for years.' I pressed my forehead to the floor and promised to listen well. The candle flame, without any wind, suddenly bent toward the dark corner.
behave:0.cnHint: 师尊告诫我，在内殿里必须____得体，否则灵气将跟随你多年。
behave:0.hook: The candle had no reason to bend — yet it did.
behave:0.line: 'How you *behave* here will echo in your spirit long after you leave.'

cent:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread the sect's trade ledger across the low table. 'Every word-herb has a price,' he said quietly. 'A fresh sprig of Breath-Root costs exactly one *cent* of cloud-silver, yet it can calm a storm inside the lungs.' I copied the figure into my own notes, careful not to smudge the ink. Outside, the bell of the western tower rang once — one beat too many.
cent:0.cnHint: 师兄解释说，一株灵草的价格仅为一____云银，但它的力量远不止于此。
cent:0.hook: The bell was supposed to ring only at dusk — not now.
cent:0.line: 'Not one *cent* of cloud-silver should be paid without checking the herb first.'

commercial:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long map of the floating markets above Cloud-Tier Nine. 'The lower sects have turned word-craft into something *commercial*,' she said, her voice carrying quiet sorrow. 'They sell healing formulas like river fish.' I looked at the bright stalls drawn on the map and felt a chill I could not explain. A crack ran silently across the ink of the highest mountain.
commercial:0.cnHint: 师尊展示了浮空市场的地图，感叹灵术已变得过于____化。
commercial:0.hook: The crack on the map spread toward the sect's own peak.
commercial:0.line: 'When word-craft becomes purely *commercial*, the words lose their living root.'

death:0.en: Xiaoxing and I sat beside the archive lamp studying the oldest scroll in the inner hall. 'Every formula has a shadow meaning,' she whispered. 'The word for deep sleep shares half its strokes with the word for *death*.' She traced the characters with one careful finger, and the lamp light shrank without any reason. We looked at each other and said nothing at all. A thin line of smoke rose from the unlit incense.
death:0.cnHint: 师妹指出，最古老的卷轴中，沉睡与____共用相同的笔画。
death:0.hook: The unlit incense was burning — no one had touched it.
death:0.line: 'The word for deep sleep and the word for *death* were once the same sign.'

escape:0.en: The practice room had no windows. Shen Wujiu placed a small cloud-glass jar on the table; inside it, one luminous word-seed spun without stopping. 'Some formulas have no *escape* once spoken,' he said. 'They bind the speaker as much as the listener.' I watched the seed spin faster and felt the air press inward. When he finally sealed the jar, my breath came back all at once.
escape:0.cnHint: 师兄警告我，某些咒语一旦说出，说话者便无法____其束缚。
escape:0.hook: The jar was sealed, but the word-seed was still spinning.
escape:0.line: 'Once you speak that formula, there is no *escape* from its weight.'

expose:0.en: Master Qingwu placed a thin sheet of spirit-paper over the old wall carving and pressed it flat. The rubbing began to *expose* a second set of characters hidden beneath the first — older strokes, sharper, full of a power the outer layer had been covering for decades. I leaned closer and felt warmth rising from the paper into my palms. Then the warmth turned cold, all at once.
expose:0.cnHint: 师尊用拓印法将墙上雕刻下面隐藏的文字____出来。
expose:0.hook: The cold spread from the paper up through my wrists toward my heart.
expose:0.line: 'This rubbing will *expose* what the sect has kept silent for thirty years.'

floor:0.en: I arrived early and found the inner hall empty. The stone *floor* was covered in faint grooves — thousands of them, worn by generations of disciples who had knelt in the same places, repeating the same words until the words became part of the rock. I knelt where the grooves were deepest and felt a low hum rise through my knees into my chest. Somewhere above me, a bell I had never heard before began to ring.
floor:0.cnHint: 我跪在内殿的石____上，感受到先辈们留下的灵气痕迹从地面涌入胸口。
floor:0.hook: No one had rung that bell — it rang itself.
floor:0.line: 'Every mark on this *floor* was left by a disciple who chose to kneel and listen.'

foundation:0.en: Shen Wujiu set the first-year primer in front of me and tapped the opening page. 'People rush to learn the flying words,' he said, 'but the *foundation* is the ten breath-forms on this page. Without them, every advanced formula you speak will crack under its own weight.' I read the first breath-form aloud and felt the floor beneath me settle deeper, as though the mountain had heard. A hairline fracture appeared in the stone beside my knee.
foundation:0.cnHint: 师兄告诫我，飞升之术的____是第一页的十种呼吸法，忽视它们将付出代价。
foundation:0.hook: The fracture in the stone was shaped exactly like the first breath-form.
foundation:0.line: 'Without this *foundation*, every word you master will eventually turn against you.'

persuade:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old ink and dried sky-herbs. I had chosen a weak word-formula for my trial, and Shen Wujiu spent the whole morning trying to *persuade* me to exchange it for a stronger one. I thanked him and held my choice. Master Qingwu watched from the doorway and said nothing.
persuade:0.cnHint: 师兄花了整个上午试图____我换一个更强的字符咒式。
persuade:0.hook: At dusk, the ink on my chosen formula began to glow on its own.
persuade:0.line: 'I want to *persuade* you, junior disciple — that word is too fragile for the ascent.'

preference:0.en: Master Qingwu set twelve word-scrolls on the stone table, each one humming with a different spiritual tone. She told us to choose freely. Xiaoxing reached for the wind-word at once, showing a clear *preference* that made Master Qingwu raise one calm eyebrow. I hesitated before the water-word for a long moment.
preference:0.cnHint: 小星拿起风字卷轴，显示出明显的____，让师尊微微扬眉。
preference:0.hook: Outside, the sea of clouds parted, and a shape no one could name rose beneath it.
preference:0.line: 'My *preference* is the wind-word — it has always answered me first.'

reliable:0.en: Shen Wujiu had copied the ascent-formula three times in clean, steady brushstrokes. Of all the senior disciples, his record of study was the most *reliable*: every word tested, every tone confirmed. I borrowed his copy before dawn and felt a quiet gratitude settle in my chest like warm tea.
reliable:0.cnHint: 师兄的修炼记录是最____的，每个字都经过验证。
reliable:0.hook: Then I found one stroke in his copy that did not match the original stone tablet.
reliable:0.line: 'A *reliable* foundation matters more than a brilliant guess — remember that on ascent day.'

suspect:0.en: A sealed word-jar had gone missing from the preparation room. Master Qingwu gathered the three of us in the hall, her voice as cool as high-altitude air. She did not accuse anyone aloud, yet her gaze lingered on me longest, and I began to *suspect* that the jar had not been lost but hidden by someone who feared its power.
suspect:0.cnHint: 师尊的目光在我身上停留最久，我开始____那个字罐并非遗失而是被藏起来了。
suspect:0.hook: By midnight the jar reappeared on my own desk, still sealed, still humming.
suspect:0.line: 'I *suspect* the word inside that jar is too strong for any one of us alone.'

yield:0.en: The cloud-cedar at the center of the courtyard was old and wise. Each spring it would *yield* a single silver leaf, which the sect pressed into a page-word of rare healing power. This morning Xiaoxing found the leaf already fallen, three months too early, curled at the root like a small closed fist.
yield:0.cnHint: 云杉树每春会____一片银叶，而今早它提前三个月落下。
yield:0.hook: Xiaoxing whispered that the leaf was still warm, as though the tree had just let it go.
yield:0.line: 'The tree will *yield* its gift only once — we must not waste a single stroke of it.'

abandon:0.en: My first attempt at the flight-word ended in silence. The characters dissolved before they could lift me, and something cold said: begin again or give up. I chose to begin again. To *abandon* the word felt like setting down a lantern in deep dark, so I pressed my brush to the page once more and breathed slowly.
abandon:0.cnHint: 放弃那个字感觉像在深暗中放下灯笼，所以我____了它，选择重新开始。
abandon:0.hook: The second attempt did not fail — it did something stranger instead.
abandon:0.line: 'Never *abandon* a word-formula mid-stroke — the energy has nowhere left to go.'

anxious:0.en: The morning of the sect's inner examination I woke before the bell. I was not afraid of the words themselves; I was *anxious* to prove that a new disciple could hold a full ascent-formula without the ink bleeding. Xiaoxing found me at my desk and set a small warm cup beside my hand without a word.
anxious:0.cnHint: 我____着要证明一个新弟子能稳住完整的飞升咒式而不让墨迹散开。
anxious:0.hook: When the bell finally rang, every candle in the hall went out at once.
anxious:0.line: 'I am *anxious* to begin — the longer we wait, the heavier the clouds feel.'

assess:0.en: Before granting permission to attempt the ascent trial, Master Qingwu asked each of us to read our word-formula aloud. She closed her eyes to *assess* the spiritual tone rather than the visible strokes, listening for cracks the way a builder tests old stone. When she opened her eyes again, she looked only at me.
assess:0.cnHint: 师尊闭目____每位弟子字符咒式的灵气音调，而非字形本身。
assess:0.hook: She said nothing — and somehow her silence carried more weight than any judgment could.
assess:0.line: 'Let me *assess* your word-tone before you climb — one false note can undo the whole ascent.'

frame:0.en: The study hall smelled of old wood and quiet ink. Along one wall hung a *frame* of carved cedar, holding the sect's founding word — a single character so old its meaning had spread into seven. Master Qingwu said the frame was not decoration; it was a boundary that kept the word from growing wild. I stood before it until my knees ached.
frame:0.cnHint: 学堂墙上有一个____，里面镶着宗门的开山字诀，师尊说它是一道边界。
frame:0.hook: At midnight, the carved cedar began to splinter from within.
frame:0.line: 'The *frame* holds the word still — step outside it and the word holds you.'

friday:0.en: In the Cloud Sea Sect, each day of the week carried a lesson. *Friday* belonged to wind-walking, and wind-walking began before the sun cleared the peaks. Shen Wujiu wrapped my ankles with strips of cloud-silk and said the word for 'rise' must be spoken on the breath, not against it. By midday I had crossed the inner courtyard twice without touching stone.
friday:0.cnHint: 每周的____是练习御风步的日子，师兄帮我缠好云丝，教我借气息吐字。
friday:0.hook: Then the wind stopped, all at once, in every direction.
friday:0.line: 'Every *Friday* the wind tests whether you have earned the week before it.'

grain:0.en: Master Qingwu placed a single *grain* of pale rice on the low table and asked me to name it. I said 'food.' She shook her head. She said it held a complete word for 'endurance' pressed inside its shell by ten seasons of sun. I spoke the name she gave me, and the grain dissolved into a faint gold light that settled on my tongue like warmth.
grain:0.cnHint: 师尊将一粒____放在桌上，说其中封印着一个完整的"忍耐"字诀。
grain:0.hook: A second grain appeared on the table, though no one had placed it there.
grain:0.line: 'One *grain* of true endurance fed into the body is worth ten years of practice.'

implication:0.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled a narrow scroll and read aloud the word for 'passage.' Then he paused. 'Feel the *implication*,' he said. The word did not only mean a door or a road; it carried inside it the suggestion of something left behind, a cost. I sat with that hidden weight until the candle burned low and the room felt smaller than before.
implication:0.cnHint: 师兄朗读了"通道"的字诀，让我感受其中的____——那个字暗含着代价与失去。
implication:0.hook: Outside, the sect gate swung open though no hand had touched it.
implication:0.line: 'Every powerful word has an *implication* — find it before the word finds you.'

incredible:0.en: Xiaoxing pressed her palms to the practice-room floor and spoke the word for 'root.' The stone beneath her hands turned briefly to soil, then back again. It lasted only a breath. She looked up at me with wide eyes. 'Was that—' she started. I told her it was *incredible*, and I meant it without any softness — roots do not grow through stone without reason, and hers had.
incredible:0.cnHint: 师妹将双掌贴地，念出字诀后石板短暂变成了泥土，我告诉她这____极了。
incredible:0.hook: Deep below us, something in the mountain answered with a slow, heavy pulse.
incredible:0.line: 'It is *incredible* — but do not let wonder slow the next word down.'

net:0.en: The lesson was on the word 'catch.' Master Qingwu demonstrated by speaking it softly over a bowl of water; the surface tightened into a fine *net* of light that held three falling petals without letting them touch the water. I tried for an hour. My net tore each time. Shen Wujiu said tearing was progress — a net that tears has at least been made.
net:0.cnHint: 师尊示范"接"字诀时，水面凝成了一张光之____，将花瓣悬在半空。
net:0.hook: When I finally held the net still, the petals spelled a word I had not yet been taught.
net:0.line: 'A *net* of words, cast with patience, will hold what force alone cannot.'

obtain:0.en: There is a rule in the Cloud Sea Sect: a disciple may not *obtain* a second word until the first has been spoken clean three hundred times. I counted every repetition in a small notebook, brushstroke by brushstroke. On the three-hundredth stroke, the ink dried gold instead of black. Xiaoxing saw it happen and said nothing, only nodded, as if she had been waiting for exactly that.
obtain:0.cnHint: 宗门规定，弟子须将第一个字诀念满三百遍，方可____第二个字诀。
obtain:0.hook: Master Qingwu appeared in the doorway before the ink had finished drying.
obtain:0.line: 'You can only *obtain* a word that you have already, in some sense, become.'

pair:0.en: Master Qingwu taught that some words must travel in a *pair* or they lose their shape. The word for 'rise' spoken alone will lift you; spoken without its partner 'return,' you may not come back down. I wrote both on the inside of my wrist with a reed brush, one above the other, as Shen Wujiu had shown me. The ink felt faintly warm all morning.
pair:0.cnHint: 师尊说有些字诀必须成____使用，"升"字若无"归"字相伴，便有去无回。
pair:0.hook: By evening, the word for 'return' had faded from my wrist and could not be found.
pair:0.line: 'Speak this word only as a *pair* — alone, it is a promise with no end.'

beautiful:0.en: Inside the Sect's archive hall, rows of glowing scrolls lined the shelves like lanterns at a festival. I reached for one, and its light spilled across my hands. Master Qingwu said the most *beautiful* formulas were also the most dangerous — their radiance a warning, not a welcome.
beautiful:0.cnHint: 师尊告诫我，那些看起来最____的法典往往隐藏着最深的危险。
beautiful:0.hook: The scroll's glow had already begun to change colour.
beautiful:0.line: 'The most *beautiful* things in this hall are the ones that will test you hardest,' said Master Qingwu.

combine:0.en: Shen Wujiu stood at the stone table, murmuring over two herb-vials. He explained that to *combine* the breath of Morning Dew with the ash of Ironcloud was rare knowledge, shared only with inner disciples. I watched in silence, my own vials untouched, wondering if I would ever be trusted with such work.
combine:0.cnHint: 师兄将两种灵药____在一起，这是只有内门弟子才能习得的秘法。
combine:0.hook: One of the vials had begun to tremble on its own.
combine:0.line: 'You must *combine* these two only when the hall bell has rung thrice,' Shen Wujiu said.

complicated:0.en: The wall of the inner study was covered in a diagram so *complicated* that I had to step back just to see its shape. Hundreds of pathways crossed and folded, each one a route through a different cloud-level. Xiaoxing stood beside me, tracing lines with her finger, naming each path in a calm, sure voice.
complicated:0.cnHint: 内室墙上那张路线图极为____，连师妹也只能辨认出其中一部分。
complicated:0.hook: One pathway on the diagram had been crossed out in fresh ink.
complicated:0.line: 'It looks *complicated*, but every path leads back to the same cloud,' said Xiaoxing.

crash:0.en: Late at night in the preparation room, I heard a sudden *crash* — one of the high shelves had given way, sending a dozen stone jars to the floor. The smell of split herbs rose sharp and sweet. I knelt to gather the pieces, and found, beneath the rubble, a sealed jar I had never seen before.
crash:0.cnHint: 夜深时，储药室传来一声____，打碎的罐子下藏着一个从未见过的密封容器。
crash:0.hook: The sealed jar was still warm, as if something inside it breathed.
crash:0.line: 'That *crash* was not caused by the shelf alone,' said Master Qingwu, at the doorway.

creature:0.en: Curled on the windowsill of the reading room was a small *creature* — no larger than my fist, its body like pale smoke held in the shape of a fox. It opened one eye when I entered, then closed it again. Xiaoxing told me it had been sleeping there for three days and had not eaten once.
creature:0.cnHint: 书房窗台上蜷伏着一只____，师妹说它已经三天没有进食了。
creature:0.hook: When I looked again, the creature had turned to face the door.
creature:0.line: 'That *creature* arrived the same morning you passed your entry trial,' said Xiaoxing softly.

crime:0.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled an old notice on the desk, its edges brown with age. It named a former disciple and listed a single *crime*: the theft of a sealed word-formula from the Sect's deepest vault. The punishment written below had been scratched out. No one, he said, knew what had become of that disciple.
crime:0.cnHint: 师兄展示了一张旧告示，上面记载了某位前任弟子所犯的____。
crime:0.hook: The name on the notice had been written, then erased, then written again.
crime:0.line: 'To take a sealed formula without leave is a *crime* no elder will forgive,' said Shen Wujiu.

deeply:0.en: I sat alone in the meditation chamber, breathing slowly, trying to reach the lower root of my energy as Master Qingwu had taught. For a long time nothing changed. Then, without warning, I felt the word-formula settle *deeply* into my body, as though it had always lived there, waiting only to be found.
deeply:0.cnHint: 在静修室中，那道法诀____地扎入我的灵根，仿佛早已等候多时。
deeply:0.hook: Outside the chamber, every candle went out at once.
deeply:0.line: 'You must let the formula sit *deeply* before you dare to use it,' Master Qingwu had said.

demonstrate:0.en: Master Qingwu asked Shen Wujiu to *demonstrate* the ascending step — the final movement before a disciple could rise above the first cloud-tier. He rose an inch from the stone floor, arms loose at his sides, face calm. The air around him hummed. I pressed the image into memory, afraid to blink.
demonstrate:0.cnHint: 师尊让师兄____飞升步法，那一刻空气中传来低沉的共鸣声。
demonstrate:0.hook: Master Qingwu's eyes were not watching Shen Wujiu — they were watching me.
demonstrate:0.line: '*Demonstrate* it slowly,' said Master Qingwu, 'so the new disciple can follow each breath.'

employment:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a pale scroll across the stone table. 'Every word has its *employment*,' she said, pressing one finger to the character for wind. 'Use it wrongly and it turns against you.' I watched the ink ripple like water disturbed by a stone, and felt my own pulse quicken with equal parts wonder and fear.
employment:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊展开卷轴，向我讲解每个字的____都有其规律，用错则会反噬。
employment:0.hook: At the scroll's edge, a single character had begun to burn on its own.
employment:0.line: 'Every word has its *employment*, and misuse is the first wound a disciple suffers.'

entire:0.en: Shen Wujiu led me through the inner hall, where the *entire* wall was covered in words carved deep into living wood. Each one glowed a soft amber, as if breathing. 'These are the healing words the Sect has gathered for three hundred years,' he said quietly. Outside, a cloud passed and every glow dimmed at once.
entire:0.cnHint: 师兄带我参观内堂，那面____刻满字符的墙壁已有三百年历史。
entire:0.hook: When the cloud passed, one character alone refused to light up again.
entire:0.line: 'The *entire* wall went dark once before — the night our last elder left and never returned.'

gift:0.en: Xiaoxing placed a small clay jar on my sleeping mat before dawn. Inside were dried word-petals, the kind that sharpen memory. 'Consider it a *gift* for your first formal lesson,' she whispered, her breath misting in the cold. I held the jar to my chest and heard, faintly, the mountain beneath us give a long, low groan.
gift:0.cnHint: 小星在我入门前夕送来一份____，是能增强记忆的干燥字瓣。
gift:0.hook: The mountain's groan came a second time, closer and more urgent than before.
gift:0.line: 'A *gift* from one new disciple to another — though the mountain tonight makes me wonder if it is wise.'

kitchen:0.en: The sect *kitchen* smelled of pine smoke and something sweeter — word-ash, the burnt remains of spoken formulas used to heat the stoves. I had been sent to grind night-root for the morning meal. My hands were still clumsy, and when I dropped the pestle it rang against the stone floor with a note that felt almost like a word itself.
kitchen:0.cnHint: 我被派去____帮忙磨夜根，那里弥漫着燃烧字诀留下的香气。
kitchen:0.hook: The ringing note hung in the air far longer than any ordinary sound should.
kitchen:0.line: 'In this *kitchen*, even the smoke carries meaning — so mind what you say aloud.'

mystery:0.en: Master Qingwu called the space between two words a *mystery* — not a gap to be filled but a silence to be understood. I sat cross-legged on the cold floor and tried to feel that silence. For one breath I thought I did: the air tightened, the lamp steadied, and a single feather drifted down from the dark ceiling above me.
mystery:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊告诉我，两个字之间的____不是空白，而是需要被理解的沉默。
mystery:0.hook: No bird had ever been seen inside the sealed inner hall before tonight.
mystery:0.line: 'The *mystery* between words is where the real power waits — do not rush past it.'

opposite:0.en: Shen Wujiu drew two words side by side on the practice board. 'These are *opposite* in meaning but share the same root stroke,' he said. 'The sect calls them twin-flames.' I copied them ten times until my brush stopped shaking. Then the candle between us split into two flames without anyone touching it.
opposite:0.cnHint: 师兄向我讲解两个意思____的字，它们却拥有相同的根笔画，门派称之为双生焰。
opposite:0.hook: Two flames from one candle — and both leaned toward me, not toward him.
opposite:0.line: '*Opposite* words are not enemies; learn them together or you will master neither.'

permanent:0.en: Master Qingwu pressed her thumb to the page and the ink turned silver. 'Nothing you write in study is *permanent*,' she said, 'except the understanding that stays in your body after the word fades.' I nodded, but when she lifted her thumb the silver did not fade. It spread instead, slowly, toward the page's edge.
permanent:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊说，习字时写下的东西没有什么是____的，真正留存的是身体对字义的领悟。
permanent:0.hook: The silver reached the edge of the page and began, impossibly, to climb the table.
permanent:0.line: 'Nothing here is *permanent* — yet somehow that ink refuses to obey me tonight.'

plenty:0.en: The storeroom held *plenty* of word-seeds: rows of small silk pouches labeled in careful brushwork, each one containing a formula compressed to a single dried syllable. Xiaoxing had told me to count them before the new moon. I reached the last shelf and found three pouches missing, their labels still tied to empty hooks, swaying gently in air that did not move.
plenty:0.cnHint: 仓库里存放着____的字种，小星让我在新月前清点，但最后一排有三袋不翼而飞。
plenty:0.hook: The empty labels bore tonight's date, written in a hand no one in the sect recognized.
plenty:0.line: 'There is *plenty* here to last a season — so tell me who counted this shelf before you.'

preserve:0.en: Inside the Sect's archive hall, I carefully arranged each scroll on its cedar shelf. Master Qingwu had taught me that we must *preserve* these ancient herbal formulas at all costs, for once lost, no elder could restore them. The ink still glowed faintly, as if the words themselves were still alive.
preserve:0.cnHint: 我在藏经阁整理古卷，努力____那些发光的草药配方。
preserve:0.hook: One scroll, however, refused to stay on its shelf.
preserve:0.line: 'We must *preserve* every word here, or the Sect loses its soul.'

procedure:0.en: Shen Wujiu stood beside the inner hall's stone altar, walking me through the morning ritual step by step. 'Each *procedure* must be followed in order,' he said quietly, 'or the spiritual energy scatters like smoke.' I repeated every motion, afraid that one wrong breath might undo the whole sequence.
procedure:0.cnHint: 师兄在石坛旁教我按照正确的____完成清晨仪式。
procedure:0.hook: At the final step, the altar stone began to crack.
procedure:0.line: 'Follow each *procedure* exactly — the altar does not forgive mistakes.'

reasonable:0.en: Master Qingwu reviewed my first month of herb-sorting in the inner storage room. 'Your progress is *reasonable*,' she said, setting down her brush with a slight nod, 'but reasonable is not enough when the Cloud Sea rises.' The lantern above us flickered once, though the air was perfectly still.
reasonable:0.cnHint: 师尊审视我一个月的成果，说我的表现还算____，但语气中带着警示。
reasonable:0.hook: The lantern above went dark before she finished speaking.
reasonable:0.line: 'Your effort is *reasonable*, yet the clouds will demand far more.'

reduction:0.en: Inside the pill room, I watched Xiaoxing measure powdered moonroot with quiet precision. She explained that even a small *reduction* in the amount — just half a breath's worth — would cause the healing pill to lose its warmth entirely. She pressed her lips together and added the tiniest pinch more.
reduction:0.cnHint: 小星在丹房里解释，药粉分量的____会让丹药失去温度。
reduction:0.hook: Her measuring spoon slipped, and the powder scattered like stars.
reduction:0.line: 'Any *reduction* in moonroot means the pill cannot heal a cold heart.'

season:0.en: Master Qingwu gathered us in the reading hall and spoke of time. 'We are entering the *season* of ascending winds,' she said, rolling open a wide chart of the mountain layers. 'During this period, your spiritual words carry twice their usual weight — and twice their usual danger.' No one made a sound.
season:0.cnHint: 师尊在书堂告诉我们，眼下正是上升风的____，修炼风险加倍。
season:0.hook: Outside, the wind arrived three days early.
season:0.line: 'In this *season*, every word you speak may rise beyond your control.'

sector:0.en: Shen Wujiu led me to the eastern *sector* of the inner hall, a zone I had never entered before. Shelves of sealed jars lined each wall, and each jar held a single written word suspended in pale mist. He said this section was reserved for words too powerful to be stored anywhere else.
sector:0.cnHint: 师兄带我进入内殿东侧的____，那里封存着力量强大的文字。
sector:0.hook: One jar bore my name written in someone else's hand.
sector:0.line: 'This *sector* holds words that chose their own containers — not the other way.'

setting:0.en: The preparation room was spare and silent: a low table, one candle, a clean brush. Master Qingwu had chosen this *setting* deliberately, she told me, because a cluttered space fills a young disciple's mind with noise before the words even arrive. I breathed in the plain stillness and felt my thoughts clear.
